title.zh: 卷35 列傳第27 鄭孝穆 崔謙 弟說 子弘度 崔猷 裴俠 薛端 薛善 弟慎
title.en: Volume 35 Biographies 27: Zheng Xiaomu; Cui Qian; younger brother Shuo;Zi Hongdu; Cui You; Pei Xia; Xue Duan; Xue Shan; younger brother Shen
title.raw: 卷35 列傳第27 鄭孝穆 崔謙 弟說 子弘度 崔猷 裴俠 薛端 薛善 弟慎 Volume 35 Biographies 27: Zheng Xiaomu; Cui Qian; younger brother Shuo;Zi Hongdu; Cui You; Pei Xia; Xue Duan; Xue Shan; younger brother Shen

sentences.zh: 鄭孝穆 崔謙 弟說 子弘度 崔猷 裴俠 薛端 薛善 弟慎

translations.literal: Zheng Xiaomu, Cui Qian, younger brother Shuo, son Hongdu, Cui You, Pei Xia, Xue Duan, Xue Shan, younger brother Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xiaomu; Cui Qian; his younger brother Shuo; Shuo's son Hongdu; Cui You; Pei Xia; Xue Duan; Xue Shan; and Shan's younger brother Shen.

sentences.zh: 鄭孝穆字道和，滎陽開封人，魏將作大匠渾之十一世孫。

translations.literal: Zheng Xiaomu, styled Dahe, was a man of Kaifeng in Xingyang; he was the eleventh-generation descendant of Hunzhi, Wei Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xiaomu, courtesy name Dahe, came from Kaifeng in Xingyang and was the eleventh in descent from Hunzhi, who had served Wei as director of palace construction.

sentences.zh: 祖敬叔，魏潁川、濮陽郡守，本邑中正。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jingshu was Administrator of Yingchuan and Puyang commanderies and native-place rectifier of his home district.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jingshu had been administrator of Yingchuan and Puyang and rectifier of his native district.

sentences.zh: 父瓊，范陽郡守，贈安東將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Qiong was Administrator of Fanyang commandery; posthumously enfeoffed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiong was administrator of Fanyang and was posthumously given the titles general who pacifies the east and inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 孝穆幼而謹厚，以清約自居。

translations.literal: Xiaomu from youth was careful and solid, and took frugal restraint as his standard.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Xiaomu was grave and steady and held himself to plain, disciplined living.

sentences.zh: 年未弱冠，涉獵經史。

translations.literal: Before he had reached twenty, he ranged through the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age he had already read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 父叔四人並早歿，昆季之中，孝穆居長。

translations.literal: His father and three uncles all died early; among the brothers Xiaomu was eldest.
translations.idiomatic: His father and three uncles had all died young, leaving Xiaomu the eldest of the brothers.

sentences.zh: 撫訓諸弟，有如同生，閨庭之中，怡怡如也。

translations.literal: He nurtured and instructed his younger brothers as though from one womb; within the inner courtyard all was harmonious delight.
translations.idiomatic: He raised and taught his younger brothers as if they shared one mother, and the household was warm and harmonious.

sentences.zh: 魏孝昌初，解褐太尉行參軍，轉司徒主簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang in Wei, he left office as acting staff officer to the Grand Commandant and was transferred to chief clerk of the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xiaochang era he entered service as acting staff officer to the grand commandant and was soon made chief clerk of the minister over the masses.

sentences.zh: 屬盜賊蜂起，除假節、龍驤將軍、別將，屢有戰功。

translations.literal: As bandits rose everywhere like swarming bees, he was appointed with provisional staff, General of Flying Dragons, and separate commander; repeatedly he had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: When bandit armies erupted across the realm he was given provisional staff, the title general of flying dragons, and a separate command, and won distinction in repeated engagements.

sentences.zh: 永安中，遷冠軍將軍、持節、都督。

translations.literal: In the Yongan era he was promoted to General Who Conquers the Enemy, bearer of the staff, and area commander.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongan he was promoted to general who conquers the enemy, given bearer of the staff, and made area commander.

sentences.zh: 從元天穆討平邢杲，進驃騎將軍、左光祿大夫、太師咸陽王長史。

translations.literal: Following Yuan Tianmu he suppressed and pacified Xing Gao, and was advanced to General of Fast Cavalry, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and chief administrator to Prince Xianyang of the Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yuan Tianmu against Xing Gao, helped crush the rebellion, and was promoted to general of fast cavalry, left grand master of splendid happiness, and chief administrator to the grand preceptor's Prince Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，從入關，除司徒左長史，領臨洮王友，賜爵永寧縣侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Xiaomu followed him through the passes and was appointed left chief administrator of the Minister over the Masses, concurrently friend to Prince Lin Tao, and enfeoffed Marquis of Yongning county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu withdrew westward, Xiaomu followed him into Guanzhong and was made left chief administrator of the minister over the masses, friend to Prince Lin Tao, and marquis of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 大統五年，行武功郡事，遷使持節、本將軍，行岐州刺史、當州都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong he acted as administrator of Wugong commandery, then was transferred to acting bearer of the staff in his existing rank, acting Inspector of Qi Province and commander of that province.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 5 he administered Wugong commandery, then was transferred to acting inspector of Qi with bearer of the staff in his existing rank and command over the province.

sentences.zh: 在任未幾，有能名。

translations.literal: In office not long, he had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Within a short time in office he had won a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 就加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was thereupon additionally made Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was then additionally appointed regular attendant of direct communication and scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 王羆時為雍州刺史，欽其善政，遣使貽書，盛相稱述。

translations.literal: Wang Pi was then Inspector of Yong Province; admiring his good governance, he sent a messenger with a letter lavishing praise upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi, then inspector of Yong Province, admired his administration and sent a messenger with a letter full of praise.

sentences.zh: 先是，所部百姓，久遭離亂，饑饉相仍，逃散殆盡。

translations.literal: Earlier, the common people under his jurisdiction had long suffered dislocation and chaos; famine followed famine, and those who fled and scattered were nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: The people of his district had long endured war and displacement; famine came one after another until almost none remained.

sentences.zh: 孝穆下車之日，戶止三千。

translations.literal: On the day Xiaomu took office, households numbered only three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaomu first arrived, registered households stood at only three thousand.

sentences.zh: 留情綏撫，遠近咸至，數年之內，有四萬家。

translations.literal: He devoted care to soothing and nurturing them; near and far all came, and within several years there were forty thousand families.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to relief and resettlement; refugees returned from near and far, and within a few years the district held forty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 每歲考績，為天下最。

translations.literal: Each year in merit review he ranked first under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year his performance review ranked highest in the realm.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，賜書曰：「知卿蒞職近畿，留心治術。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor commended him and granted a letter saying: "I know that since you took office near the capital you have kept your mind on methods of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai praised him and wrote: "Since you took up office in the capital region you have applied yourself to governing.

sentences.zh: 凋弊之俗，禮教興行；

translations.literal: In a wasted and ruined custom, ritual teaching rises and goes forward;
translations.idiomatic: Where custom had withered, you have revived ritual and education;

sentences.zh: 厭亂之民，繈負而至。

translations.literal: people weary of disorder come carrying infants on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: people exhausted by chaos return carrying their children on their backs.

sentences.zh: 昔郭伋政成幷部，賈琮譽重冀方，以古方今，彼有慚德。

translations.literal: In olden days Guo Xian's governance succeeded in Bing Province and Jia Cong's fame weighed heavy in Ji Region — comparing antiquity with today, they would feel ashamed before your virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xian once governed Bing with success and Jia Cong won renown in Ji — set against you, even those ancients would blush at their lesser merit.

sentences.zh: 」於是徵拜京兆尹。

translations.idiomatic: [closing quote]

sentences.zh: 十五年，梁雍州刺史、岳陽王蕭詧稱藩來附，時議欲遣使，盛選行人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was summoned and appointed Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was then recalled and appointed metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 太祖歷觀內外，無逾孝穆者。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Xiao Cha of Liang, Inspector of Yong Province and Prince of Yueyang, submitted as a vassal and came over; at the time the court debated sending envoys and carefully selected traveling officers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15, Xiao Cha, Liang's inspector of Yong and prince of Yueyang, submitted as a vassal; the court debated whom to send and searched carefully for the right envoy.

sentences.zh: 十六年，乃假孝穆散騎常侍，持節策拜詧為梁王。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor surveyed within and without, and none surpassed Xiaomu.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai looked through the court and the provinces and found no one better suited than Xiaomu.

sentences.zh: 使還稱旨，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he thereupon provisionally made Xiaomu Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, bearer of the staff, to invest Cha as Prince of Liang by edict.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 he provisionally appointed Xiaomu regular attendant of scattered cavalry and bearer of the staff to invest Cha as prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 是年，太祖總戎東討，除大丞相府右長史，封金鄉縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: When the mission returned and accorded with the imperial intent, he was promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Three Departments, with the added title Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the embassy returned to the court's satisfaction, he was promoted to grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal in three departments, with the added title regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 軍次潼關，命孝穆與左長史長孫儉、司馬楊寬、尚書蘇亮、諮議劉孟良等分掌衆務。

translations.literal: That year the Grand Progenitor took overall command in an eastern campaign; Xiaomu was appointed right chief administrator of the great chief minister's office, enfeoffed Baron of Jinxiang county with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marched east at the head of the army; Xiaomu was made right chief administrator of the great chief minister's office and enfeoffed baron of Jinxiang with two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 仍令孝穆引接關東歸附人士，幷品藻才行而任用之。

translations.literal: The army halted at Tong Pass; Xiaomu was ordered together with left chief administrator Zhangsun Jian, marshal Yang Kuan, secretary Su Liang, adviser Liu Mengliang, and others to divide and manage the multitude of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Tong Pass, Xiaomu was ordered with left chief administrator Zhangsun Jian, marshal Yang Kuan, secretary Su Liang, adviser Liu Mengliang, and others to divide the staff work among them.

sentences.zh: 孝穆撫納銓敘，咸得其宜。

translations.literal: He was further ordered to receive and connect with men of talent from east of the Pass who submitted, and together to appraise conduct and ability and appoint them to office.
translations.idiomatic: He was also charged with welcoming eastern defectors, assessing their talent and character, and placing them in suitable posts.

sentences.zh: 大將軍達奚武率衆經略漢中，以孝穆為梁州刺史，以疾不之部。

translations.literal: Xiaomu soothed, received, and ranked them; all obtained their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaomu settled, enrolled, and ranked them so that each man found the right appointment.

sentences.zh: 拜中書令，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: Great General Daxi Wu led the host to pacify Hanzhong; Xiaomu was made Inspector of Liang Province but, owing to illness, did not go to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Great general Daxi Wu marched to secure Hanzhong; Xiaomu was appointed inspector of Liang but did not take up the post because of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾免。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat and granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the Secretariat and given the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為子，增邑通一千戶。

translations.literal: Soon, because of illness, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long illness forced his retirement.

sentences.zh: 晉公護為雍州牧，辟為別駕，又以疾固辭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, Xiaomu was given the added titles General of Fast Cavalry and Opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, advanced in rank to viscount, and his fief increased in all to one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Xiaomu was additionally made general of fast cavalry and opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, raised to viscount, and given a combined fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 武成二年，徵拜御伯中大夫，徙授御正。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu was Governor of Yong Province and recruited him as vice administrator, but again because of illness he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, then governor of Yong Province, tried to recruit him as vice administrator, but illness again made him refuse firmly.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，出為宜州刺史，轉華州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wucheng he was summoned and appointed Middle Grand Master of the Imperial Elder, then transferred and appointed Imperial Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng year 2 he was recalled and made middle grand master of the imperial elder, then transferred to imperial rectifier.

sentences.zh: 五年，除虞州刺史，轉陝州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding he went out as Inspector of Yi Province, then was transferred to Inspector of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 3 he left the capital as inspector of Yi, then was transferred to inspector of Hua.

sentences.zh: 頻歷數州，皆有政績。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Inspector of Yu Province, then transferred to Inspector of Shaan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was made inspector of Yu, then transferred to inspector of Shaan.

sentences.zh: 復以疾篤，屢乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he held several provinces, and in all there was administrative achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He served in one province after another, and everywhere left a record of good governance.

sentences.zh: 入為少司空。

translations.literal: Again, because his illness was severe, repeatedly he begged to resign his bones.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew grave he repeatedly asked leave to retire.

sentences.zh: 卒於位，時年六十。

translations.literal: He entered the court as Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加鄭梁北豫三州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in office, aged sixty at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted his former office and additionally made Inspector of Zheng, Liang, and Northern Yu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he kept his last office and was additionally given the titles inspector of Zheng, Liang, and Northern Yu.

sentences.zh: 子詡嗣。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Zhen.

sentences.zh: 歷位納言，為聘陳使。

translations.literal: His son Xu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 後至開府儀同三司、大將軍、邵州刺史。

translations.literal: Through the ranks he reached Remonstrator and served as envoy on a mission to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to remonstrator and served as envoy on a mission to Chen.

sentences.zh: 詡弟譯，於隋文帝有翊贊功，開皇初，又追贈孝穆大將軍、徐兗等六州刺史，改諡曰文。

translations.literal: Later he reached Opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, Great General, and Inspector of Shao Province.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, great general, and inspector of Shao.

sentences.zh: 譯幼聰敏，涉獵羣書，尤善音樂，有名于時。

translations.literal: Xu's younger brother Yi had assisting and supporting merit with Emperor Wen of Sui; at the beginning of Kaihuang he further posthumously enfeoffed Xiaomu Great General and Inspector of Xu, Yan, and the other six provinces, and changed the posthumous title to Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's younger brother Yi had helped establish Emperor Wen of Sui; at the opening of Kaihuang he had Xiaomu posthumously made great general and inspector of Xu, Yan, and five other provinces, and changed his posthumous title to Wen.

sentences.zh: 世宗詔令事輔城公。

translations.literal: Yi from youth was clever and keen, ranged through the multitude of books, and was especially skilled in music; he had a name in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was clever from childhood, read widely, and was especially gifted in music; his name was known throughout the age.

sentences.zh: 及高祖卽位。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong issued an edict ordering him to serve the Duke of Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong ordered him to attend the duke of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 除都督，稍遷御正下大夫，頗被顧待。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne.

sentences.zh: 東宮建，以譯為宮尹下大夫，特被太子親愛。

translations.literal: He was appointed area commander and gradually promoted to Lower Grand Master of Imperial Rectification, and was much favored and attended.
translations.idiomatic: He was made area commander and gradually rose to lower grand master of imperial rectification, winning steady favor at court.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，為聘齊使副。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established, Yi was made Lower Grand Master as palace intendant and was especially beloved by the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern palace was established Yi was made lower grand master and palace intendant, and the crown prince came to love him dearly.

sentences.zh: 及太子西征，多有失德，王軌、宇文孝伯等以聞，高祖大怒，宮臣親幸者，咸被譴責，譯坐除名。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande he served as deputy envoy on a mission to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande year 2 he served as deputy envoy on a mission to Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 後例復官，仍拜吏部下大夫。

translations.literal: When the crown prince marched west on campaign there were many lapses in virtue; Wang Gui, Yuwen Xiaobo, and others reported them, and Emperor Wu was greatly angered — palace officials who were close favorites were all reprimanded, and Yi was dismissed and stripped of name.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince campaigned west he behaved badly in many ways; Wang Gui, Yuwen Xiaobo, and others reported it, and Emperor Wu flew into a rage — every favored palace attendant was rebuked, and Yi was stripped of rank and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，授開府儀同大將軍、內史中大夫，封歸昌縣公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: Later, by precedent he was restored to office and again appointed Lower Grand Master of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Later, under the usual rule, he was restored to office and again made lower grand master of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 旣以恩舊，任遇甚重，朝政機密，竝得參詳。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he was appointed Opener of the Way Equal in Great General and Middle Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat, enfeoffed Duke of Guichang county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded he was made opener of the Way equal in great general and middle grand master of the palace secretariat, and enfeoffed duke of Guichang with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋遷內史上大夫，進爵沛國公。

translations.literal: Because he was an old favorite by grace, his appointment and favor were very weighty; state secrets of court governance he together obtained and deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: As an old confidant he was heavily favored and was admitted to the most confidential affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 上大夫之官，自譯始也。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Upper Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat and advanced in rank to Duke of the Pei State.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to upper grand master of the palace secretariat and raised to duke of Pei.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝大漸，御正下大夫劉昉乃與譯謀，以隨公受遺輔少主。

translations.literal: The office of upper grand master began with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The rank of upper grand master began with Yi.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝執政，拜柱國、大丞相府長史，內史如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan fell gravely ill, Lower Grand Master of Imperial Rectification Liu Fang then plotted with Yi that the Duke of Sui receive the testamentary charge and assist the young lord.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan lay gravely ill, lower grand master Liu Fang plotted with Yi to put the duke of Sui in charge of the regency and support the young emperor.

sentences.zh: 尋進位上柱國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui took power, Yi was appointed Pillar of State and chief administrator of the great chief minister's office, with the palace secretariat as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui seized power, Yi was made pillar of state and chief administrator of the great chief minister's office while keeping his secretariat post.

sentences.zh: 崔謙字士遜，博陵安平人也。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced in rank to Upper Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to upper pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 祖辯，魏平遠將軍、武邑郡守。

translations.literal: Cui Qian, styled Shixun, was a man of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qian, courtesy name Shixun, came from Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 父楷，散騎常侍、光祿大夫、殷州刺史，贈侍中、都督冀定相三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bian was Wei General Who Pacifies the Distance and Administrator of Wuyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bian had served Wei as general who pacifies the distance and administrator of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 謙幼聰敏，神彩嶷然。

translations.literal: His father Kai was Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Inspector of Yin Province; posthumously enfeoffed Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief over the military affairs of Ji, Ding, and Xiang provinces, General of Fast Cavalry, Equal in Three Departments, and Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kai had been regular attendant of scattered cavalry, grand master of splendid happiness, and inspector of Yin; posthumously he was given palace attendant, commander-in-chief over Ji, Ding, and Xiang, general of fast cavalry, equal in three departments, and inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 及長，深沉有識量。

translations.literal: Qian from youth was clever and keen; his spirit and bearing stood lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was clever from childhood, with a commanding presence.

sentences.zh: 歷觀經史，不持章句，志在博聞而已。

translations.literal: When grown he was deep and reserved, with judgment and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he was grave and far-seeing.

sentences.zh: 每覽經國緯民之事，心常好之，未嘗不撫卷歎息。

translations.literal: He ranged through the classics and histories but did not cling to chapter-and-phrase study; his aim was broad hearing only.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and histories without pedantic glossing; he sought breadth of learning rather than narrow expertise.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，解褐著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Whenever he read affairs of ordering the state and binding the people, in his heart he always delighted in them and never failed to stroke the scroll and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he read about governing the realm and caring for the people he would unroll the text and sigh with longing.

sentences.zh: 從太宰元天穆討邢杲，破之，以功授輔國將軍、太中大夫，遷平東將軍、尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he left office as assistant editor in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiaochang he entered service as assistant editor in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 賀拔勝出鎮荊州，以謙為行臺左丞。

translations.literal: Following Grand Preceptor Yuan Tianmu he attacked Xing Gao, defeated him, and by merit was appointed General Who Assists the State and Grand Master of the Palace, then transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Director of the Palace in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He followed grand preceptor Yuan Tianmu against Xing Gao, helped defeat him, and for his service was made general who assists the state and grand master of the palace, then transferred to general who pacifies the east and director of the palace in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 勝雖居方岳之任，至於安輯夷夏，綱紀衆務，皆委謙焉。

translations.literal: Heba Sheng went out to garrison Jing Province and made Qian left assistant of the mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Sheng took charge of Jing Province he appointed Qian left assistant of the mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 謙亦盡其智能，以相匡弼。

translations.literal: Although Sheng held the responsibility of a frontier pillar, as to settling and harmonizing barbarians and Chinese, maintaining order over the multitude of affairs — all were entrusted to Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Though Sheng held a great frontier command, Qian handled the work of pacifying barbarians and Chinese alike and keeping every affair in order.

sentences.zh: 勝有聲南州，謙之力也。

translations.literal: Qian likewise exhausted his intelligence and ability to assist and correct him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian in turn gave all his talent to advising and supporting him.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武將備齊神武之逼，乃詔勝引兵赴洛。

translations.literal: Sheng had fame in the southern provinces — Qian's strength was in that.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's reputation in the south was largely Qian's doing.

sentences.zh: 軍至廣州，帝已西遷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei was about to prepare against Gao Huan's pressure, he issued an edict ordering Sheng to lead troops to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu prepared to resist Gao Huan's pressure, he ordered Sheng to march to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 勝乃遲疑，將旋所鎮。

translations.literal: When the army reached Guangzhou, the emperor had already moved west.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the army reached Guangzhou, the emperor had already fled westward.

sentences.zh: 謙謂勝曰：「昔周室不造，諸侯釋位；

translations.literal: Sheng then hesitated and was about to turn back to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng wavered and prepared to withdraw to his post.

sentences.zh: 漢道中微，列藩盡節。

translations.literal: Qian said to Sheng: "In olden days the house of Zhou met misfortune and the feudal lords relinquished their posts;
translations.idiomatic: Qian told Sheng: "When the Zhou house fell into crisis, the feudal lords set aside their own posts;

sentences.zh: 今皇家多故，主上蒙塵，寔忠臣枕戈之時，義士立功之日也。

translations.literal: when the Han Way declined in its middle age, the border princes all kept faith to the end.
translations.idiomatic: when the Han dynasty waned, the frontier princes held loyal to the last.

sentences.zh: 公受方面之重，總宛、葉之衆，若杖義而動，首唱勤王，天下聞風，孰不感激。

translations.literal: Now the royal house has many troubles and the sovereign suffers dust on the road — truly this is the hour for loyal ministers to sleep upon their spears and for men of righteousness to establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: Now the throne is in turmoil and the emperor is in exile — this is the hour when loyal ministers should take up arms and men of honor win distinction.

sentences.zh: 誠宜順義勇之志，副遐邇之心，倍道兼行，謁帝關右。

translations.literal: You bear the weight of a regional command and command the hosts of Wan and Ye; if you move by righteousness and take the lead in raising troops to restore the ruler, when all under Heaven hear the wind, who will not be moved?
translations.idiomatic: You hold a great regional command and the armies of Wan and Ye; if you march in the name of righteousness and lead the call to restore the emperor, who under Heaven would not rally to you?

sentences.zh: 然後與宇文行臺，同心協力，電討不庭。

translations.literal: Truly you ought to follow the will of righteous courage, answer the hearts of near and far, double the road and march together, and pay homage to the emperor west of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: You should heed the call of loyal courage, satisfy the hopes of the realm, force the march day and night, and present yourself before the emperor in the west.

sentences.zh: 則桓、文之勳，復興於茲日矣。

translations.literal: Then together with the Yuwen mobile headquarters, with one heart and combined strength, strike the rebellious like lightning.
translations.idiomatic: Then, joining Yuwen's mobile headquarters, you can move as one and strike the rebels like lightning.

sentences.zh: 舍此不為，中道而退，便恐人皆解體，士各有心。

translations.literal: Then the merit of Huan and Wen would be revived on this day.
translations.idiomatic: Then the achievement of Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Qi could be renewed in our own day.

sentences.zh: 一失事機，後悔何及。

translations.literal: Abandon this and do not act; turn back halfway — then I fear every man will lose heart and officers will each go their own way.
translations.idiomatic: If you abandon this course and retreat halfway, every soldier will lose heart and each officer will follow his own impulse.

sentences.zh: 」勝不能用，而人情果大騷動。

translations.literal: Once the opportunity is lost, regret will not reach it." Sheng could not employ him, and as expected popular sentiment was greatly unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Miss this chance and regret will come too late." Sheng would not heed him, and morale collapsed as Qian had warned.

sentences.zh: 還未至州，州民鄧誕引侯景軍奄至，勝與戰，敗績，遂將麾下數百騎南奔於梁。

translations.literal: Before he had yet reached the province, the provincial people under Deng Dan led Hou Jing's army to arrive suddenly; Sheng fought them, was defeated, and thereupon led several hundred horsemen of his command south in flight to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached Jing, local leader Deng Dan brought Hou Jing's army down on him; Sheng was defeated and fled south to Liang with a few hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 謙亦與勝俱行。

translations.literal: Qian likewise went together with Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qian went into exile with him.

sentences.zh: 及至梁，每乞師赴援。

translations.literal: When they reached Liang, repeatedly he begged troops to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Liang he repeatedly pleaded for troops to relieve the north.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝雖不為出軍，而嘉勝等志節，竝許其還國。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang although he did not send out an army, yet admired the will and integrity of Sheng and the others, and together permitted their return to their state.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang would not send an army, but he admired Sheng and his companions for their loyalty and allowed them all to return home.

sentences.zh: 乃分謙先還，且通鄰好。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Qian back first, and at the same time opened communication of neighborly good will.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qian back ahead of the others while opening friendly relations with the north.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝見謙甚悅，謂之曰：「卿出萬死之中，投身江外，今得生還本朝，豈非忠貞之報也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei, seeing Qian, was greatly pleased and said to him: "You went out from amid ten thousand deaths and cast yourself beyond the river; now you obtain life and return to this court — is this not the reward of loyalty and steadfastness?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei received Qian with delight and said: "You escaped death beyond the Yangtze and have returned alive to the court — is this not loyalty repaid?

sentences.zh: 」太祖素聞謙名，甚禮之。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor had long heard Qian's name and treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had long known Qian by reputation and received him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 乃授征西將軍、金紫光祿大夫，賜爵千乘縣男。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed General Who Campaigns West, Supervising Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and enfeoffed Baron of Qiansheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was then made general who campaigns west, supervising grand master with the golden seal and purple ribbon, and enfeoffed baron of Qiansheng.

sentences.zh: 及勝至，拜太師，以謙有毗輔之功，又授太師長史。

translations.literal: When Sheng arrived and was appointed Grand Tutor, because Qian had merit in close assistance, he was also appointed chief administrator of the Grand Tutor's office.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Sheng returned and was made grand tutor, Qian was rewarded for his close counsel with the post of chief administrator of the grand tutor's office.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，從太祖擒竇泰，戰沙苑，竝有功。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong he followed the Grand Progenitor in capturing Dou Tai and fighting at Shaye, and in both had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 3 he followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in capturing Dou Tai and fighting at Shaye, winning distinction in both.

sentences.zh: 進爵為子，遷車騎大將軍、右光祿大夫，拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to viscount; he was transferred to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and appointed Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to viscount, made grand general of chariots and cavalry and right grand master of splendid happiness, and appointed right assistant director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 謙明練時事，及居樞轄，時論以為得人。

translations.literal: Qian was clear and practiced in current affairs; when he took a central post, opinion of the time held that the right man had been chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was shrewd and experienced in public affairs; once he held a central post, contemporaries agreed the court had found the right man.

sentences.zh: 四年，從太祖解洛陽圍，仍經河橋戰，加定州大中正、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the Grand Progenitor in relieving the siege of Luoyang and also fought at He Bridge; he was additionally made grand rectifier of Ding Province and Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in lifting the siege of Luoyang and fighting at He Bridge, and was additionally made grand rectifier of Ding and inspector of Ying.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授車騎大將軍、儀同三司，又破柳仲禮於隨郡，討平李遷哲於魏興，並有功。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Three Departments; he also defeated Liu Zhongli at Sui commandery and suppressed Li Qianzhe at Weixing, all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he was made grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal in three departments; he also defeated Liu Zhongli in Sui commandery and suppressed Li Qianzhe at Weixing.

sentences.zh: 進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、直州刺史，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General of Fast Cavalry, Opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, and Inspector of Zhi Province, and granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of fast cavalry, opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, and inspector of Zhi, and given the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝初，轉利州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gong of Wei's reign, he was transferred to Inspector of Li Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Gong's reign he was transferred to inspector of Li Province.

sentences.zh: 謙性明悟，深曉政術，又勤於理務，民訟雖繁，未嘗有懈倦之色。

translations.literal: Qian by nature was bright and penetrating, deeply versed in the arts of government, and diligent in administration; though civil suits were many, he never showed weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was bright by nature, deeply skilled in governance, and tireless in office; though lawsuits piled up, he never showed fatigue.

sentences.zh: 吏民以是敬而愛之。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners for this reason both respected and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike respected and loved him for it.

sentences.zh: 時有蜀人賈晃遷舉兵作亂，率其黨圍逼州城。

translations.literal: At the time a man of Shu named Jia Huangqian raised troops in rebellion and led his faction to surround and press the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a Shu native named Jia Huangqian rebelled and led his followers to besiege the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 謙倉卒分部，纔得千許人，便率拒戰。

translations.literal: Qian hastily divided his forces; gathering only about a thousand men, he led them to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Qian hastily mustered his forces; with barely a thousand men he marched out to meet them.

sentences.zh: 會梁州援兵至，遂擒晃遷，餘人乃散。

translations.literal: When relief troops from Liang Province arrived, he captured Huangqian and the rest dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: When reinforcements from Liang Province arrived, he captured Huangqian and the rest scattered.

sentences.zh: 謙誅其渠帥，餘竝原之。

translations.literal: Qian executed the ringleaders and pardoned all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Qian executed the ringleaders and pardoned everyone else.

sentences.zh: 旬日之間，遂得安輯。

translations.literal: Within ten days order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the province was pacified.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，進爵作唐縣公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, his rank was advanced to Duke of Zuotang county.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Shizong's reign he was raised to duke of Zuotang.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，遷安州總管、隨應等十一州甑山上明魯山三鎮諸軍事、安州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding he was transferred to Area Commander of An Province, commander of military affairs for eleven provinces including Sui and Ying, the three garrisons of Zengshan, Shangming, and Lushan, and Inspector of An Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 2 he was made area commander of An, given command over eleven provinces including Sui and Ying, the three garrisons of Zengshan, Shangming, and Lushan, and appointed inspector of An.

sentences.zh: 四年，加大將軍，進爵武康郡公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was further made Great General and advanced to Duke of Wukang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was further made great general and raised to duke of Wukang commandery.

sentences.zh: 謙性至孝，少喪父，殆將滅性。

translations.literal: Qian was deeply filial by nature; he lost his father in youth and nearly destroyed himself in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was profoundly filial; he lost his father young and nearly died of grief.

sentences.zh: 與弟〔說〕特相友愛，雖復年事竝高，名位各重，所有資產，皆無私焉。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Shuo were especially close and affectionate; though both were advanced in years and each held weighty rank and title, they shared all property without private distinction.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Shuo were unusually close; though both were old and each held high rank, they held all their property in common without private hoarding.

sentences.zh: 其居家嚴肅，動遵禮度。

translations.literal: Their household was run with severity, and in every action they observed ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Their household was sternly ordered, and in every act they kept to ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 曠與說子弘度等，竝奉其遺訓云。

translations.literal: Kuang and Shuo's son Hongdu, among others, all followed his precepts, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang and Shuo's son Hongdu, among others, all lived by his teaching, it is said.

sentences.zh: 曠少溫雅，仁而汎愛。

translations.literal: Kuang from youth was gentle and refined, benevolent and broad in affection.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang from youth was mild and refined, generous and warmly affectionate.

sentences.zh: 釋褐中外府記室。

translations.literal: Upon entering office he was made recording secretary of the Central and External Office.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as recording secretary of the central and external office.

sentences.zh: 大象末，位至開府儀同大將軍，淅州刺史。

translations.literal: By the end of the Daxiang era he had reached Opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, Great General, and Inspector of Xi Province.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Daxiang era he had risen to opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, great general, and inspector of Xi.

sentences.zh: 說本名士約，少鯁直，有節概，膂力過人，尤工騎射。

translations.literal: Shuo's original name was Shiyue; from youth he was blunt and upright, possessed moral backbone, his physical strength surpassed other men, and he was especially skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo had originally been named Shiyue; from youth he was blunt and upright, strong in principle, unusually powerful, and especially skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 釋褐領軍府錄事，轉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Upon entering office he was made recording officer of the Army Guard headquarters and transferred to consulting staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as recording officer in the army guard headquarters and was transferred to consulting staff officer.

sentences.zh: 及賀拔勝出牧荊州，以說為假節、冠軍將軍、防城都督。

translations.literal: When Heba Sheng went out to administer Jing Province, he made Shuo acting bearer of the staff, General Who Conquers the Enemy, and defense-city area commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Sheng took charge of Jing Province he made Shuo acting bearer of the staff, general who conquers the enemy, and defense-city area commander.

sentences.zh: 又隨勝奔梁，復自梁歸國。

translations.literal: He again followed Sheng in flight to Liang and later returned from Liang to their state.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Sheng into exile in Liang and later returned home from Liang.

sentences.zh: 授衛將軍﹑都督，封安昌縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Guard and area commander, enfeoffed Viscount of Anchang county with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of the guard and area commander, and enfeoffed viscount of Anchang with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 從太祖復弘農，戰沙苑，皆有功。

translations.literal: Following the Grand Progenitor he recovered Hongnong and fought at Shaye, with merit in both.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in retaking Hongnong and fighting at Shaye, winning distinction in both.

sentences.zh: 進爵為侯，增邑八百戶，除京兆郡守。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to marquis, his fief increased by eight hundred households, and he was appointed Administrator of Jingzhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to marquis, given eight hundred additional households, and appointed administrator of Jingzhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 累遷帥都督、撫軍將軍、通直散騎常侍、大都督、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、都官尚書、定州大中正，改封安固縣侯，增邑三百戶，賜姓宇文氏，幷賜名說焉。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to division commander, General Who Pacifies the Army, Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Scattered Cavalry, Chief Area Commander, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Three Departments, Minister of Justice, and grand rectifier of Ding Province; his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Angu county with three hundred added fief households; he was granted the surname Yuwen and also given the name Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to division commander, general who pacifies the army, regular attendant of direct communication and scattered cavalry, chief area commander, grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal in three departments, minister of justice, and grand rectifier of Ding; his title was changed to marquis of Angu with three hundred more households, he was given the surname Yuwen, and he also received the name Shuo.

sentences.zh: 進爵驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中，進爵萬年縣公，增邑通前二千四百戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General of Fast Cavalry and Opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, made Palace Attendant, and advanced to Duke of Wannian county with a total fief of twenty-four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of fast cavalry and opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, made palace attendant, and raised to duke of Wannian with a combined fief of twenty-four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 除隴州刺史，遷總管涼甘瓜三州諸軍事、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Inspector of Long Province and transferred to Area Commander over military affairs of the three provinces of Liang, Gan, and Gua, and Inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed inspector of Long and transferred to area commander over Liang, Gan, and Gua and inspector of Liang.

sentences.zh: 說蒞政強毅，百姓畏之。

translations.literal: In governing, Shuo was forceful and resolute, and the common people feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo governed with force and resolution, and the common people feared him.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲東征，以說為行軍長史。

translations.literal: When Prince Xian of Qi marched east, Shuo was made chief administrator of the marching army.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xian of Qi campaigned east, Shuo was made chief administrator of the field army.

sentences.zh: 軍還，除使持節、崇德安義等十三防熊和

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs for the thirteen defense posts including Chongde and Anyi, and for Xiong and He
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was given bearer of the staff and command over the thirteen defense posts including Chongde and Anyi and over Xiong and He

translations.literal: (Zhōng) [emended: Zhōng]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Zhōng]

sentences.zh: 〔中〕等三州諸軍事，崇德防主，加授大將軍，改封安平縣公。

translations.literal: 〔Zhōng〕 and the other three prefectures, commander of Chongde defense, additionally appointed Great General, and his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Anping county.
translations.idiomatic: and Zhong and the other three prefectures, made commander of Chongde defense, additionally appointed great general, and enfeoffed duke of Anping.

sentences.zh: 建德四年卒，時年六十四。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Jiande, aged sixty-four at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiande year 4 at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈鄜延丹綏長五州刺史，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted governorship over the five provinces of Fu, Yan, Dan, Sui, and Chang; posthumous title: Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made governor of Fu, Yan, Dan, Sui, and Chang; his posthumous title was Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子弘度，猛毅有父風。

translations.literal: His son Hongdu was fierce and resolute with his father's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongdu was bold and resolute and had his father's manner.

sentences.zh: 大象末，上柱國、武鄉郡公。

translations.literal: By the end of Daxiang he was Upper Pillar of State and Duke of Wuxiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Daxiang he was upper pillar of state and duke of Wuxiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 崔猷字宣猷，博陵安平人，漢尚書寔之十二世孫也。

translations.literal: Cui You, styled Xuanyou, was a man of Anping in Boling, twelfth-generation descendant of Han Minister of Works Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Cui You, courtesy name Xuanyou, came from Anping in Boling and was twelfth in descent from Han minister of works Cui Shi.

sentences.zh: 祖挺，魏光州刺史、泰昌縣子，贈輔國將軍、幽州刺史，諡曰景。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ting was Northern Wei Inspector of Guang Province and Viscount of Taichang county; posthumously made General Who Assists the State and Inspector of You Province; posthumous title: Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ting had been Northern Wei inspector of Guang and viscount of Taichang; posthumously he was made general who assists the state and inspector of You; his posthumous title was Jing.

sentences.zh: 父孝芬，左光祿大夫、儀同三司，兼吏部尚書，為齊神武所害。

translations.literal: His father Xiaofen was Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Equal in Three Departments, concurrently Minister of Personnel; he was killed by Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiaofen had been left grand master of splendid happiness and equal in three departments and concurrent minister of personnel; Gao Huan had him killed.

sentences.zh: 猷少好學，風度閒雅，性鯁正，有軍國籌略。

translations.literal: You from youth loved learning, had an easy and refined bearing, was blunt and upright in nature, and possessed strategems for army and state.
translations.idiomatic: You loved learning from youth, had an easy and refined bearing, was upright by nature, and possessed talent for military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 釋褐員外散騎侍郎，領大行臺郎中。

translations.literal: Upon entering office he was made Regular Attendant Outside the Regular Establishment of Scattered Cavalry and concurrently director of the Great Mobile Headquarters office.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as regular attendant outside the regular establishment of scattered cavalry and concurrently director of the great mobile headquarters office.

sentences.zh: 尋為吏部尚書李神儁所薦，拜通直散騎侍郎，攝尚書駕部郎中。

translations.literal: Soon he was recommended by Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun, appointed Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Scattered Cavalry, and acting director of the Chariot Department of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun recommended him; he was made regular attendant of direct communication and scattered cavalry and acting director of the chariot department in the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，除征虜將軍、司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai he was appointed General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Attendant in the Secretariat of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Putai he was appointed general who subdues the barbarians and attendant in the secretariat of the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 旣遭家難，遂間行入關。

translations.literal: Having suffered the calamity of his family, he then traveled by secret routes into the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After the disaster that struck his family he stole by hidden paths into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 及謁魏孝武，哀動左右，帝為之改容。

translations.literal: When he had audience with Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, his grief moved those around him and the emperor changed countenance for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he had audience with Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, his grief moved everyone present and the emperor's face changed for him.

sentences.zh: 旣退，帝目送之曰：「忠孝之道，萃此一門。

translations.literal: After he withdrew, the emperor watched him depart and said: "The way of loyalty and filial piety is gathered in this one family.
translations.idiomatic: As he withdrew, the emperor watched him go and said, "Loyalty and filial piety are gathered in this one house.

sentences.zh: 」卽以本官奏門下事。

translations.literal: " Thereupon with his existing office he reported matters to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: With his existing rank he was charged with reporting to the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大統初，兼給事黃門侍郎，封平原縣伯，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong he was concurrently made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gates and enfeoffed Baron of Pingyuan county with eight hundred fief households.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Datong he was concurrently made attendant gentleman of the yellow gates and enfeoffed baron of Pingyuan with eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 二年，正除黃門，加中軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year he was formally appointed to the Yellow Gates, with the added title General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was formally appointed to the yellow gates and additionally made general of the central army.

sentences.zh: 擒竇泰，復弘農，破沙苑，猷常以本官從軍典文翰。

translations.literal: In capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and breaking Shayuan, You constantly followed on campaign in his existing office, managing documents and dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: In the capture of Dou Tai, the recovery of Hongnong, and the victory at Shayuan, You followed on campaign in his existing office and handled documents and dispatches.

sentences.zh: 五年，除司徒左長史，加驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education, with the added title General of Fast Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was made left chief administrator of the minister of education and additionally general of fast cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時太廟初成，四時祭祀，猶設俳優角抵之戲，其郊廟祭官，多有假兼。

translations.literal: At the time the Imperial Ancestral Temple had just been completed; at the seasonal sacrifices entertainers and wrestling performances were still staged, and many of the suburban and temple sacrificial officers held concurrent acting appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial ancestral temple had just been completed; seasonal sacrifices still featured acrobats and wrestling, and many suburban and temple officers held concurrent acting posts.

sentences.zh: 猷屢上疏諫，書奏，竝納焉。

translations.literal: You repeatedly submitted memorials remonstrating; his letters and reports were all accepted.
translations.idiomatic: You repeatedly memorialized against this, and every proposal was accepted.

sentences.zh: 遷京兆尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 時婚姻禮廢，嫁娶之辰，多舉音樂。

translations.literal: At the time marriage ritual had fallen into disuse; on wedding days music was often played at length.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage ritual had fallen into disuse, and weddings were often celebrated with lavish music.

sentences.zh: 又廛裏富室，衣服奢淫，乃有織成文繡者。

translations.literal: Moreover, wealthy households in the market wards wore extravagant and licentious clothing, even woven brocades with embroidered patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families in the wards also dressed with extravagant luxury, even wearing brocades woven with embroidered designs.

sentences.zh: 猷又請禁斷，事亦施行。

translations.literal: You again requested that these be forbidden and cut off, and the measure was also carried out.
translations.idiomatic: You again asked that these practices be forbidden, and the order was enforced.

sentences.zh: 與盧辯等剏修六官。

translations.literal: Together with Lu Bian and others he created and revised the Six Offices system.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Lu Bian and others he helped create and revise the six offices system.

sentences.zh: 十二年，除大都督、驃騎將軍、淅州刺史，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Chief Area Commander, General of Fast Cavalry, and Inspector of Xi Province, with the added titles Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was made chief area commander, general of fast cavalry, and inspector of Xi, with the added titles grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal in three departments.

sentences.zh: 十四年，侯景據河南歸款，遣行臺王思政赴之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Hou Jing held Henan and offered submission; the Grand Progenitor dispatched Mobile Headquarters Commissioner Wang Sizheng to go to him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 Hou Jing held Henan and offered submission; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent mobile headquarters commissioner Wang Sizheng to meet him.

sentences.zh: 太祖與思政書曰：「崔宣猷智略明贍，有應變之才，若有所疑，宜與量其可不。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor wrote to Sizheng: "Cui Xuanyou is intelligent and broad in strategy and has talent for adapting to change; if you have doubts, you should consult with him and weigh what can or cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai wrote Wang Sizheng: "Cui Xuanyou is shrewd, far-seeing, and quick to adapt; if you are uncertain about anything, consult him and weigh what can and cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 」思政初

translations.literal: " Sizheng at first
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Sizheng at first

translations.literal: (Lǐng) [emended: Dùn]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Dùn]

sentences.zh: 〔頓〕兵襄城，後欲於潁川為行臺治所，遣使人魏仲奉啟陳之。

translations.literal: 〔Dùn〕 troops at Xiangcheng; later he wished to make Yingchuan the seat of the mobile headquarters and sent messenger Wei Zhong with a memorial setting this forth.
translations.idiomatic: stationed his troops at Xiangcheng; later he wanted to move the mobile headquarters to Yingchuan and sent Wei Zhong with a memorial explaining the plan.

sentences.zh: 幷致書於猷論將移之意。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to You discussing his intention to relocate.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote You to discuss the proposed move.

sentences.zh: 猷復書曰：「夫兵者，務在先聲後實，故能百戰百勝，以弱為強也。

translations.literal: You replied in a letter: "In warfare one must put prestige before substance; thus one can win a hundred battles in a hundred engagements and turn weakness into strength.
translations.idiomatic: You wrote back: "In war one must put reputation before force; that is how a weaker side wins a hundred fights in a hundred and turns weakness into strength.

sentences.zh: 但襄城控帶京洛，寔當今之要地，如有動靜，易相應接。

translations.literal: But Xiangcheng controls and links the capital region; it is truly a key place of the present day. If anything occurs, response and liaison are easy.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangcheng commands the Luoyang region and is truly the key point of the day; if anything happens, relief and coordination are easy.

sentences.zh: 潁川旣鄰寇境，又無山川之固，賊若充斥，徑至城下。

translations.literal: Yingchuan borders the enemy frontier and lacks the protection of mountains and rivers; if bandits swarm forth, they will come straight to the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchuan lies on the enemy border and has no mountain barriers; if raiders pour in, they will reach the walls at once.

sentences.zh: 輒以愚情，權其利害，莫若頓兵襄城，為行臺治所，潁川置州，遣郭賢鎮守。

translations.literal: Setting forth my humble view and weighing advantage and harm, nothing is better than stationing the army at Xiangcheng as the seat of the mobile headquarters, establishing a province at Yingchuan, and posting Guo Xian to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing the matter as best I can, it would be better to keep the army at Xiangcheng as headquarters, make Yingchuan a province, and post Guo Xian to hold it.

sentences.zh: 則表裏膠固，人心易安，縱有不虞，豈能為患。

translations.literal: Then inner and outer defenses would be firmly linked, hearts would easily be at ease, and even if something unforeseen occurred, how could it become a disaster?
translations.idiomatic: Then inner and outer lines would be secure, morale would stay steady, and even if something went wrong, how could it become a real disaster?

sentences.zh: 」仲見太祖，具以啟聞。

translations.literal: " Zhong saw the Grand Progenitor and reported the whole in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhong saw Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and reported everything in full.

sentences.zh: 太祖卽遣仲還，令依猷之策。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor immediately sent Zhong back and ordered that You's plan be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai at once sent Zhong back and ordered that You's plan be followed.

sentences.zh: 思政重啟，求與朝廷立約：賊若水攻，乞一周為斷；

translations.literal: Sizheng memorialized again, requesting to establish an agreement with the court: if the enemy attacks by water, he asked one week as the limit;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng memorialized again and asked the court for a formal agreement: if the enemy attacked by water, he wanted one week as the limit;

sentences.zh: 陸攻，請三歲為期。

translations.literal: for attack by land, he requested three years as the term.
translations.idiomatic: if by land, three years.

sentences.zh: 限內有事，不煩赴援。

translations.literal: Within the limit if anything occurred, he would not trouble them to send relief.
translations.idiomatic: Within those limits he would not ask the court for relief.

sentences.zh: 過此以往，惟朝廷所裁。

translations.literal: Beyond that, only the court would decide.
translations.idiomatic: After that, the court alone would decide.

sentences.zh: 太祖以思政旣親其事，兼復固請，遂許之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor, since Sizheng was personally involved in the affair and pressed hard besides, thereupon granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wang Sizheng was personally involved and pressed the request hard, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai granted it.

sentences.zh: 及潁川沒後，太祖深追悔焉。

translations.literal: When Yingchuan fell afterward, the Grand Progenitor deeply regretted it in retrospect.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingchuan later fell, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai deeply regretted having agreed.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以疾去職。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he left office on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 he left office because of illness.

sentences.zh: 屬大軍東征，太祖賜以馬輿，命隨軍，與之籌議。

translations.literal: When the great army marched east, the Grand Progenitor granted him a carriage-and-horses and ordered him to follow the army and take part in planning.
translations.idiomatic: When the great army marched east, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai gave him a carriage and horses and ordered him to follow the campaign and join the planning.

sentences.zh: 十七年，進侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、本州大中正，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was advanced to Palace Attendant, General of Fast Cavalry, Opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, and grand rectifier of his native province; he was granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he was made palace attendant, general of fast cavalry, opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, and grand rectifier of his native province, and given the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 世宗卽位，徵拜御正中大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, You was summoned and appointed Middle Grand Master of Imperial Rectification.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, You was summoned and made middle grand master of imperial rectification.

sentences.zh: 時依《周禮》稱天王，又不建年號，猷以為世有澆淳，運有治亂，故帝王以之沿革，聖哲因時制宜。

translations.literal: At the time, following the Rites of Zhou, the sovereign was called Heavenly King and no era name was established; You held that generations have their shallow and pure phases and the times have their order and disorder, and therefore emperors and kings have altered institutions accordingly, while sages adapted measures to the times.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court, following the Rites of Zhou, styled the ruler Heavenly King and used no reign title; You argued that ages differ in refinement and corruption and times in order and chaos, so rulers change institutions and sages adapt policy to circumstance.

sentences.zh: 今天子稱王，不足以威天下，請遵秦漢稱皇帝，建年號。

translations.literal: Today the Son of Heaven is styled king, which is insufficient to awe the realm; I request that we follow Qin and Han in styling him emperor and establishing an era name.
translations.idiomatic: He said the title of king was too weak to command the realm and asked that Qin and Han precedent be followed by styling the ruler emperor and establishing a reign title.

sentences.zh: 朝議從之。

translations.literal: Court deliberation followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 武成二年，除司會中大夫，御正如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wucheng he was appointed Middle Grand Master of the Coordinator of Affairs; his post as imperial rectifier remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng year 2 he was made middle grand master of the coordinator of affairs while keeping his post as imperial rectifier.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，陳將華皎來附，晉公護議欲南伐，公卿莫敢正言。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, Chen general Hua Jiao came over in allegiance; Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu proposed a southern campaign, and none among the highest ministers dared speak against it.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year 2 the Chen general Hua Jiao defected; Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu proposed a southern campaign, and none of the chief ministers dared object.

sentences.zh: 猷獨進曰：「前歲東征，死傷過半，比雖加撫循，而瘡痍未復。

translations.literal: You alone advanced and said: "Last year's eastern campaign killed and wounded more than half our force; though we have since added consolation and care, the wounds are not yet healed.
translations.idiomatic: You alone stepped forward and said, "Last year's eastern campaign killed and wounded more than half our army; though we have since tried to heal the damage, the wounds are not yet mended.

sentences.zh: 近者長星為災，乃上玄所以垂鑒誡也。

translations.literal: Recently the baleful star has brought calamity — this is how Heaven above shows admonition and warning.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the baleful star has appeared — Heaven is warning us.

sentences.zh: 誠宜修德以禳天變，豈可窮兵極武而重其譴負哉？

translations.literal: We should truly cultivate virtue to avert heaven's changes — how can we exhaust the armies and push warfare to the limit and again bear heaven's reproach?
translations.idiomatic: We should cultivate virtue to avert heaven's warning — how can we exhaust our armies again and invite further reproach?

sentences.zh: 今陳氏保境息民，共敦鄰好。

translations.literal: Now the Chen house keeps its territory and lets the people rest; we share a good neighborly bond.
translations.idiomatic: Chen keeps its borders and lets its people rest; we are bound by good neighborly relations.

sentences.zh: 無容違盟約之重，納其叛臣，興無名之師，利其土地。

translations.literal: One cannot lightly violate the weight of treaties, accept their rebel ministers, raise an army without just cause, and covet their land.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot lightly break a solemn treaty, harbor their defectors, launch an unjust war, and seize their territory.

sentences.zh: 詳觀前載，非所聞也。

translations.literal: Looking carefully at earlier records, this is not what one hears of.
translations.idiomatic: A careful reading of earlier history shows nothing of the kind.

sentences.zh: 」護不從。

translations.literal: " Yuwen Hu did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu would not listen.

sentences.zh: 其後水軍果敗，而裨將元定等遂沒江南。

translations.literal: Afterward the naval army was indeed defeated, and assistant generals Yuan Ding and others were lost south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet was defeated as he had warned, and assistant generals such as Yuan Ding were lost in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 建德四年，出為同州司會。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiande, he was sent out as provincial accountant of Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiande he was posted as provincial accountant of Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 六年，征拜小司徒，加上開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was summoned as lesser minister of education, with the added rank of opening-office grand general with precedence equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was recalled as lesser minister of education and given the added title of opening-office grand general with precedence equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝踐極，以猷前代舊齒，授大將軍，進爵汲郡公，增邑通前三千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, because You was an elder of the previous dynasty, he was appointed grand general, advanced to Duke of Ji commandery, and his fief was increased to three thousand households in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, You was treated as a senior figure of the former dynasty: he was made grand general, raised to Duke of Ji commandery, and his fief was brought to three thousand households in all.

sentences.zh: 開皇四年卒，諡曰明。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Kaihuang; his posthumous title was Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Kaihuang and was posthumously titled Ming.

sentences.zh: 子仲方，字不齊，早知名，機神穎悟，文學優敏。

translations.literal: His son Zhongfang, styled Buqi, was early known for his reputation; he was quick-witted and sharp, and excelled in letters.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongfang, courtesy name Buqi, won early renown for his quick mind and literary skill.

sentences.zh: 大象末，儀同大將軍、司玉下大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daxiang era he held the ranks of grand general with distinguished records and lower grand master of the Jade Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he was grand general with distinguished records and lower grand master of the Jade Office.

sentences.zh: 裴俠字嵩和，河東解人也。

translations.literal: Pei Xia, styled Songhe, was a native of Jie in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xia, courtesy name Songhe, came from Jie in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖思齊，舉秀才，拜議郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Siqi passed the provincial examination and was appointed gentleman consultant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Siqi passed the provincial examination and became a gentleman consultant.

sentences.zh: 父欣，博涉經史，魏昌樂王府司馬、西河郡守，贈晉州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xin was broadly versed in the classics and histories; he served as marshal of the household of Prince Le of Wei-chang and as administrator of Xihe commandery, and was posthumously given the post of inspector of Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin read widely in the classics and histories, served as marshal of the household of Prince Le of Wei-chang and as administrator of Xihe commandery, and was posthumously made inspector of Jin Province.

sentences.zh: 俠幼而聰慧，有異常童。

translations.literal: Xia from youth was intelligent and clever, unlike ordinary children.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Xia was unusually bright and precocious.

sentences.zh: 年十三，遭父憂，哀毀有若成人。

translations.literal: At age thirteen he suffered his father's death and mourned with the grief and self-denial of an adult.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen, when his father died, he mourned with the restraint and grief of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿，舉秀才。

translations.literal: The province recruited him as chief clerk, and he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial authorities enlisted him as chief clerk, and he succeeded at the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 魏正光中，解巾奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era of Wei he entered service as attendant at court.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguang era of Wei he entered office as an attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 稍遷員外散騎侍郎、義陽郡守。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to external scattered-cavalry attendant-in-ordinary and administrator of Yiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to external scattered-cavalry attendant-in-ordinary and administrator of Yiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，俠執其使人，焚其赦書。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Xia seized his emissary and burned his amnesty edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Xia arrested his envoy and burned the amnesty edict he carried.

sentences.zh: 魏孝莊嘉之，授輕車將軍、東郡太守，帶防城別將。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei commended him and appointed him general of light chariots and administrator of Dong commandery, with the added post of vice general for city defense.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei praised him and made him general of light chariots and administrator of Dong commandery, also appointing him vice general for city defense.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武與齊神武有隙，征河南兵以備之，俠率所部赴洛陽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei fell out with Gao Huan, Henan troops were levied for defense, and Xia led his command to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei broke with Gao Huan, troops were called up in Henan for defense, and Xia led his men to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 授建威將軍，左中郎將。

translations.literal: He was appointed general who establishes might and left central commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who establishes might and left central commandant.

sentences.zh: 俄而孝武西遷，俠將行而妻子猶在東郡。

translations.literal: Before long Xiaowu moved west; Xia was about to go, but his wife and children were still in Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Emperor Xiaowu moved west. Xia was ready to follow, but his wife and children remained in Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 滎陽鄭偉謂俠曰：「天下方亂，未知烏之所集。

translations.literal: Zheng Wei of Xingyang said to Xia: "The realm is in chaos, and no one knows where the crows will gather.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Wei of Xingyang told Xia, "The empire is in turmoil, and no one knows where things will settle.

sentences.zh: 何如東就妻子，徐擇木焉。

translations.literal: Why not go east to your wife and children and slowly choose your perch?"
translations.idiomatic: Why not go east to your family first and wait to see where to land?"

sentences.zh: 」俠曰：「忠義之道，庸可忽乎！

translations.literal: " Xia said: "The way of loyalty and righteousness — how can one neglect it!
translations.idiomatic: " Xia replied, "How can one set aside loyalty and righteousness!

sentences.zh: 吾旣食人之祿，寧以妻子易圖也。

translations.literal: I have already received another's salary; how could I change my course for wife and children?"
translations.idiomatic: I have already accepted another's pay — would I abandon my duty for my wife and children?"

sentences.zh: 」遂從入關。

translations.literal: " He then followed into Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the court into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 賜爵清河縣伯，除丞相府士曹參軍。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Earl of Qinghe county and appointed staff officer of the personnel section in the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Earl of Qinghe county and appointed a personnel staff officer in the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，領鄉兵從戰沙苑，先鋒陷陣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong he led local militia into battle at Shayuan and, as vanguard, broke through the enemy lines.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong he led local militia at Shayuan and, fighting in the vanguard, broke the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 俠本名協，至是，太祖嘉其勇決，乃曰「仁者必有勇」，因命改焉。

translations.literal: Xia's original name had been Xie; at this time the Grand Progenitor praised his courage and decisiveness, saying, "The benevolent must have courage," and ordered the name changed.
translations.idiomatic: Xia had originally been named Xie. The Grand Progenitor now praised his courage and resolve, quoted the saying "The benevolent must have courage," and had his name changed.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵為侯，邑八百戶，拜行臺郎中。

translations.literal: For his merit he was advanced to marquis with a fief of eight hundred households and appointed bureau director of the field secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was raised to marquis with a fief of eight hundred households and made bureau director of the field secretariat.

sentences.zh: 王思政鎮玉壁，以俠為長史。

translations.literal: When Wang Sizheng garrisoned Yubi, he appointed Xia chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sizheng held Yubi, he made Xia his chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 未幾為齊神武所攻。

translations.literal: Before long the place was attacked by Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gao Huan attacked the fortress.

sentences.zh: 神武以書招思政，思政令俠草報，辭甚壯烈。

translations.literal: Gao Huan wrote to win Sizheng over; Sizheng had Xia draft the reply, and its language was very bold and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan wrote trying to win Wang Sizheng over. Sizheng had Xia draft the reply, and the wording was fiercely defiant.

sentences.zh: 太祖善之，曰：「雖魯連無以加也。」

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor approved and said: "Even Lu Zhonglian could add nothing to this."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor praised it and said, "Not even Lu Zhonglian could have improved on this."

sentences.zh: 除河北郡守。

translations.literal: He was appointed administrator of Hebei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He took office as administrator of Hebei commandery.

sentences.zh: 俠躬履儉素，愛民如子，所食唯菽麥鹽菜而已。

translations.literal: Xia personally practiced frugality and simplicity, loved the people as his children, and ate only beans, wheat, salt, and vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Xia lived plainly, treated the people like his own children, and ate nothing but beans, grain, salt, and vegetables.

sentences.zh: 吏民莫不懷之。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners all held him in affection.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike loved him.

sentences.zh: 此郡舊制，有漁獵夫三十人以供郡守。

translations.literal: By the commandery's old regulation, thirty fishing and hunting laborers were kept to serve the administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Under an old commandery rule, thirty men were assigned to fish and hunt for the administrator's table.

sentences.zh: 俠曰：「以口腹役人，吾所不為也。

translations.literal: Xia said: "To put people to work for one's belly — that I will not do."
translations.idiomatic: Xia said, "I will not make men serve my appetite."

sentences.zh: 」乃悉罷之。

translations.literal: " He then abolished them all.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the practice entirely.

sentences.zh: 又有丁三十人，供郡守役使。

translations.literal: There were also thirty adult males assigned to run the administrator's errands.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty corvée laborers were also assigned to the administrator's personal service.

sentences.zh: 俠亦不以入私，並收庸直，為官市馬。

translations.literal: Xia likewise did not use them for private ends; he collected their service fees and used them to buy horses for the government.
translations.idiomatic: Xia would not use them privately either. He took their service fees and bought horses for the government.

sentences.zh: 歲月旣積，馬遂成羣。

translations.literal: As the months accumulated, the horses eventually became a herd.
translations.idiomatic: Over time the purchases grew into a whole herd of horses.

sentences.zh: 去職之日，一無所取。

translations.literal: On the day he left office he took nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office he took nothing with him.

sentences.zh: 民歌之曰：「肥鮮不食，丁庸不取，裴公貞惠，為世規矩。

translations.literal: The people sang of him: "Rich food he would not eat, corvée labor he would not take — Lord Pei's integrity and kindness is a model for the age."
translations.idiomatic: The people sang, "He ate no dainties, took no corvée pay — Lord Pei's upright kindness sets the standard for the world."

sentences.zh: 」俠嘗與諸牧守俱謁太祖。

translations.literal: " Xia once paid audience to the Grand Progenitor together with the various regional governors.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when Xia joined the regional governors in audience before the Grand Progenitor,

sentences.zh: 太祖命俠別立，謂諸牧守曰：「裴俠清慎奉公，為天下之最，今衆中有如俠者，可與之俱立。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor ordered Xia to stand apart and said to the governors: "Pei Xia is pure and cautious in serving the public — the best in the realm. If any among you is like Xia, you may stand with him."
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Progenitor had Xia stand apart and told the governors, "Pei Xia is the most scrupulous and dutiful official in the empire. If any of you are his equal, step forward and stand beside him."

sentences.zh: 」衆皆默然，無敢應者。

translations.literal: " All were silent; none dared respond.
