translations.idiomatic: Everyone fell silent. No one stepped forward.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃厚賜俠。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor then richly rewarded Xia.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor then gave Xia a rich reward.

sentences.zh: 朝野嘆服，號為獨立君。

translations.literal: Court and countryside sighed in admiration and called him the Independent Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country admired him and nicknamed him the Independent Lord.

sentences.zh: 俠又撰九世伯祖貞侯潛傳，以為裴氏清公，自此始也，欲使後生奉而行之，宗室中知名者，咸付一通。

translations.literal: Xia also compiled a biography of his ninth-generation grand-uncle, Marquis Zhen Hou Qian, holding that the Pei clan's record of pure public service began with him; he wanted later generations to follow it, and every well-known member of the clan received a copy.
translations.idiomatic: Xia also wrote a biography of his ninth-generation grand-uncle, Marquis Zhen Hou Qian, treating him as the founder of the Pei family's tradition of upright service, and gave copies to every prominent kinsman so later generations might follow the example.

sentences.zh: 從弟伯鳳、世彥，時並為丞相府佐，笑曰：「人生仕進，須身名竝裕。

translations.literal: His cousins Bofeng and Shiyan, then both aides in the chancellor's office, laughed and said: "In advancing through office one needs both body and name to prosper together.
translations.idiomatic: His cousins Bofeng and Shiyan, both then aides in the chancellor's office, laughed and said, "If you want to get ahead in office, you need comfort as well as reputation.

sentences.zh: 清苦若此，竟欲何為？

translations.literal: Being pure and hard like this — what do you ultimately intend?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you hope to gain by living in such austerity?"

sentences.zh: 」俠曰：「夫清者莅職之本，儉者持身之基。

translations.literal: " Xia said: "Purity is the root of holding office; frugality is the foundation of maintaining oneself.
translations.idiomatic: " Xia answered, "Integrity is the basis of office, and frugality is the basis of conduct.

sentences.zh: 況我大宗，世濟其美，故能：存，見稱於朝廷；

translations.literal: Moreover, in our great clan excellence has been handed down through generations, so that while alive one is praised at court
translations.idiomatic: Our great house has handed down this virtue for generations, so that in life a man is praised at court

sentences.zh: 沒，流芳於典策。

translations.literal: and after death one's good name flows into the historical records.
translations.idiomatic: and after death his name lives on in the histories.

sentences.zh: 今吾幸以凡庸，濫蒙殊遇，固其窮困，非慕名也。

translations.literal: Now I am fortunate, though merely ordinary, to have undeservedly received special favor; being poor is only natural — this is not pursuit of fame.
translations.idiomatic: I am only an ordinary man who has been favored beyond his deserts. My poverty is natural, not a bid for reputation.

sentences.zh: 志在自修，懼辱先也。

translations.literal: My aim is self-cultivation, for I fear disgracing my ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: I mean only to discipline myself, lest I shame my forebears.

sentences.zh: 翻被嗤笑，知復何言。

translations.literal: Instead I am mocked — what more can I say?"
translations.idiomatic: And now I am laughed at — what more is there to say?"

sentences.zh: 」伯鳳等慚而退。

translations.literal: " Bofeng and the others withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Bofeng and the others withdrew, ashamed.

sentences.zh: 九年，入為大行臺郎中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he entered service as bureau director of the great field secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he entered office as bureau director of the great field secretariat.

sentences.zh: 居數載，出為郢州刺史，加儀同三司，尋轉

translations.literal: After several years he was sent out as inspector of Ying Prefecture, given the added rank of precedence equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and soon transferred to
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was posted as inspector of Ying Prefecture, given precedence equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and soon transferred to

translations.literal: (Shi) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Tuo]

sentences.zh: 〔拓〕州刺史，征拜雍州別駕。

translations.literal: 〔Tuo〕 Prefecture inspector, and was summoned as deputy governor of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: governor of Tuo Prefecture, then recalled as deputy governor of Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，除司邑下大夫，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為公，增邑通前一千六百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, Xia was appointed lower grand master of the Office of Domains, given the added ranks of senior grand general and opening-office status equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, advanced to duke, and his fief was increased to one thousand six hundred households in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Xia was made lower grand master of the Office of Domains, given the added titles of senior grand general and opening-office status equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, raised to duke, and his fief was brought to one thousand six hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 遷民部中大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand master of the Ministry of Population.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to grand master of the Ministry of Population.

sentences.zh: 時有姦吏，主守倉儲，積年隱沒至千萬者，及俠在官，勵精發摘，數旬之內，姦盜略盡。

translations.literal: At the time corrupt officials in charge of granaries had for years concealed losses reaching into the tens of millions; when Xia took office he worked diligently to investigate, and within several ten-day periods corruption and theft were largely eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt granary officials had for years concealed losses running into the tens of millions. Once Xia took office he investigated relentlessly, and within a few weeks most of the fraud had been cleared away.

sentences.zh: 轉工部中大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand master of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to grand master of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 有大司空掌錢物典李貴乃於府中悲泣。

translations.literal: Li Gui, registrar of money and goods under the grand minister of works, began weeping in the office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui, the registrar of funds and stores under the grand minister of works, burst into tears in the office.

sentences.zh: 或問其故。

translations.literal: Someone asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why,

sentences.zh: 對曰：「所掌官物，多有費用，裴公清嚴有名，懼遭罪責，所以泣耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "The official goods under my charge have much unauthorized expenditure. Lord Pei is renowned for stern purity, and I fear punishment — that is why I weep."
translations.idiomatic: he said, "There has been much improper spending from the funds I manage. Lord Pei is famous for his severity, and I am afraid of being punished — that is why I am crying."

sentences.zh: 」俠聞之，許其自首。

translations.literal: " When Xia heard of it, he allowed him to confess voluntarily.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia heard this, he allowed Gui to confess on his own.

sentences.zh: 貴言隱費錢五百萬。

translations.literal: Gui reported concealed expenditures of five million cash.
translations.idiomatic: Gui admitted to five million in hidden expenses.

sentences.zh: 俠之肅遏姦伏，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Xia's stern suppression of corruption and hidden wrongdoing was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Xia's stern suppression of hidden corruption was always like this.

sentences.zh: 子祥，性忠謹，有治劇才。

translations.literal: His son Xiang was by nature loyal and careful and had a talent for handling difficult cases.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiang was loyal, careful, and skilled at handling hard cases.

sentences.zh: 少為成都令，清不及俠，斷決過之。

translations.literal: In youth he served as magistrate of Chengdu; in purity he did not equal Xia, but in judicial decisions he surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he served as magistrate of Chengdu. He was not as austere as Xia, but he surpassed him in deciding cases.

sentences.zh: 後除長安令，為權貴所憚。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed magistrate of Chang'an and was feared by the powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as magistrate of Chang'an, he was feared by the great families.

sentences.zh: 遷司倉下大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to lower grand master of the Office of Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to lower grand master of the Office of Granaries.

sentences.zh: 俠之終也，遂以毀卒。

translations.literal: When Xia died, Xiang died from grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia died, Xiang died of grief.

sentences.zh: 祥弟肅，貞亮有才藝。

translations.literal: Xiang's younger brother Su was upright, bright, and talented in the arts.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's younger brother Su was upright, talented, and accomplished in the arts.

sentences.zh: 天和中，舉秀才，拜給事中士。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era he passed the provincial examination and was appointed attendant gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhe era he passed the provincial examination and became an attendant gentleman.

sentences.zh: 稍遷御正大夫，賜爵胡原縣子。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to grand master of the imperial correctors and granted the title Viscount of Huyuan county.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to grand master of the imperial correctors and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Huyuan county.

sentences.zh: 薛端字仁直，河東汾陰人也，本名沙陀。

translations.literal: Xue Duan, styled Renzhi, was a native of Fenyin in Hedong; his original name was Shatuo.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Duan, courtesy name Renzhi, came from Fenyin in Hedong. His original name was Shatuo.

sentences.zh: 魏雍州刺史、汾陰侯辨之六世孫。

translations.literal: He was the sixth-generation descendant of Bian, Marquis of Fenyin and inspector of Yong Province of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was the sixth-generation descendant of Bian, Marquis of Fenyin and Wei inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 代為河東著姓。

translations.literal: For generations the clan was a prominent surname in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had been a leading clan in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 高祖謹，泰州刺史、內都坐大官、涪陵公。

translations.literal: His high ancestor Jin was inspector of Tai Province, chief palace provisioner, and Duke of Fuling.
translations.idiomatic: His distant ancestor Jin had been inspector of Tai Province, chief palace provisioner, and Duke of Fuling.

sentences.zh: 曾祖洪隆，河東太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Honglong was administrator of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Honglong had governed Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 以隆兄洪阼尚魏文〔成〕帝女西河公主，有賜田在馮翊，洪隆子麟駒徙居之，遂家于馮翊之夏陽焉。

translations.literal: Because Honglong's elder brother Hongzha had married Princess Xihe, daughter of Emperor Wen[cheng] of Wei, and had been granted land in Fenyang, Honglong's son Linju moved there, and the family then settled at Xiayang in Fenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Honglong's elder brother Hongzha had married Princess Xihe, daughter of Emperor Wen of Wei, and received granted land in Fenyang. Honglong's son Linju moved there, and the family settled at Xiayang in Fenyang.

sentences.zh: 麟駒舉秀才，拜中書博士，兼主客郎中，贈河東太守。

translations.literal: Linju passed the provincial examination, was appointed doctor of the secretariat and concurrently master-of-guests attendant-in-ordinary, and was posthumously given the post of administrator of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Linju passed the provincial examination, became doctor of the secretariat and concurrently master-of-guests attendant-in-ordinary, and was posthumously made administrator of Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 父英集，通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His father Yingji was attendant-in-ordinary for direct communication.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingji was an attendant-in-ordinary for direct communication.

sentences.zh: 端少有志操。

translations.literal: Duan from youth had aspiration and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Duan had strong principles.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂，居喪合禮。

translations.literal: When his father died he observed mourning according to the rites.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he observed mourning properly.

sentences.zh: 與弟裕，勵精篤學，不交人事。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Yu he applied himself diligently to learning and did not engage in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Yu studied hard and kept aloof from worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 年十七，司空高乾辟為參軍，賜爵汾陰縣男。

translations.literal: At age seventeen the grand minister Gao Gan recruited him as staff officer and granted him the title Baron of Fenyin county.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen the grand minister Gao Gan recruited him as a staff officer and enfeoffed him as Baron of Fenyin county.

sentences.zh: 端以天下擾亂，遂棄官歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Because the realm was in turmoil, Duan abandoned office and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: With the empire in turmoil, Duan resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，太祖令大都督薛崇禮據龍門，引端同行。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, the Grand Progenitor ordered grand area commander Xue Chongli to hold Longmen and took Duan along with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, the Grand Progenitor ordered grand area commander Xue Chongli to hold Longmen and took Duan with him.

sentences.zh: 崇禮尋失守，遂降東魏。

translations.literal: Chongli soon lost the fortress and surrendered to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chongli soon lost the position and surrendered to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 東魏遣行臺薛循義、都督乙干貴率衆數千西度，據楊氏壁。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei sent field secretariat Xue Xunyi and area commander Yigan Gui leading several thousand men west across the river to occupy Yangshi Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent field secretariat Xue Xunyi and area commander Yigan Gui with several thousand men west across the river to seize Yangshi Stockade.

sentences.zh: 端與宗親及家僮等先在壁中，循義乃令其兵逼端等東度。

translations.literal: Duan, with his clansmen and household servants, was already in the fortress; Xunyi then ordered his troops to drive Duan and the others east across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Duan, his kinsmen, and household servants were already inside the fortress when Xunyi ordered his troops to force them east across the river.

sentences.zh: 方欲濟河，會日暮，端密與宗室及家僮等叛之。

translations.literal: Just as they were about to cross the river, dusk fell; Duan secretly joined with kinsmen of the imperial clan and household servants in rebellion against them.
translations.idiomatic: As they were about to cross, night fell; Duan secretly rallied the imperial clansmen and household servants and turned against them.

sentences.zh: 循義遣騎追，端且戰且馳，遂入石城柵，得免。

translations.literal: Xunyi sent cavalry in pursuit; Duan fought as he rode and entered the Stone City stockade, escaping capture.
translations.idiomatic: Xunyi sent cavalry in pursuit; Duan fought as he fled and reached the Stone City stockade, where he escaped.

sentences.zh: 柵中先有百家，端與並力固守。

translations.literal: A hundred households were already in the stockade; Duan joined them and they held firm together.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred households were already in the stockade; Duan joined them and they held out together.

sentences.zh: 貴等數來慰喻，知端無降意，遂拔還河東。

translations.literal: Gui and the others came repeatedly to reassure and persuade him; seeing Duan had no intent to surrender, they withdrew to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and the others came again and again to reassure and persuade him; when they saw Duan would not surrender, they withdrew to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 東魏又遣其將賀蘭懿、南汾州刺史薛琰達守楊氏壁。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei also sent its generals Helan Yi and Southern Fen Prefecture inspector Xue Yanda to hold Yang's Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei also sent its generals Helan Yi and Xue Yanda, inspector of Southern Fen, to hold Yang's Fortress.

sentences.zh: 端率其屬，並招喻村民等，多設奇以臨之。

translations.literal: Duan led his followers and also summoned and persuaded the village people, setting many stratagems to press them.
translations.idiomatic: Duan rallied his followers, summoned and reassured the villagers, and used many ruses to pressure the enemy.

sentences.zh: 懿等疑有大軍，便卽東遁，爭船溺死者數千人。

translations.literal: Yi and the others suspected a large army was present and immediately fled east; in the scramble for boats several thousand men drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and the others suspected a large army was at hand and fled east at once; in the scramble for boats several thousand men drowned.

sentences.zh: 端收其器械，復還楊氏壁。

translations.literal: Duan gathered their weapons and returned again to Yang's Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Duan collected their weapons and returned to Yang's Fortress.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣南汾州刺史蘇景恕鎮之。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor sent Southern Fen Prefecture inspector Su Jingshu to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent Su Jingshu, inspector of Southern Fen, to garrison the fortress.

sentences.zh: 降書勞問，徵端赴闕，以為大丞相府戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: A letter of commendation was sent summoning Duan to court; he was made registrar in the grand chancellor's household.
translations.idiomatic: A letter of commendation summoned Duan to court, and he was made registrar in the grand chancellor's household.

sentences.zh: 從擒竇泰，復弘農，戰沙苑，竝有功。

translations.literal: He took part in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and fighting at Shachuan, all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and fighting at Shachuan, all with distinction.

sentences.zh: 加冠軍將軍、中散大夫，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: He was given the additional ranks of general who conquers and palace attendant, and advanced in enfeoffment to baron.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the added titles of general who conquers and palace attendant and was raised to baron.

sentences.zh: 轉丞相東合祭酒，加本州大中正，遷兵部郎中，改封文城縣伯，加使持節、平東將軍、吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to libationer of the eastern pavilion in the chancellor's office, given the added post of grand selector of his native province, promoted to director in the ministry of war, changed in enfeoffment to Baron of Wencheng county, and given the added ranks of bearer of staff, general who pacifies the east, and director in the ministry of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He became libationer of the chancellor's eastern pavilion, was made grand selector of his native province, rose to director in the ministry of war, was re-enfeoffed as Baron of Wencheng county, and received the added ranks of bearer of staff, general who pacifies the east, and director in the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 端性強直，每有奏請，不避權貴。

translations.literal: Duan was stern and upright by nature; whenever he memorialized the throne he did not avoid the powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: Duan was stern and upright by nature; in every memorial he never shrank from the powerful and noble.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，故賜名端，欲令名質相副。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor commended this and therefore bestowed on him the name Duan, wishing name and substance to match.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai commended this and therefore gave him the name Duan, wanting his name and character to match.

sentences.zh: 自居選曹，先盡賢能，雖貴遊子弟，才劣行薄者，未嘗升擢之。

translations.literal: From the time he held office in the selection bureau, he always put the capable first; even among the sons of noble families, if talent was poor and conduct thin, he never promoted them.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held office in the selection bureau, he always put the capable first; even sons of noble families with poor talent and thin conduct he never promoted.

sentences.zh: 每啟太祖云：「設官分職，本康時務，苟非其人，不如曠職。

translations.literal: Each time he reported to Grand Progenitor: "To appoint offices and divide duties is fundamentally to bring ease to the age's affairs; if the man is not right for the post, better to leave the office vacant.
translations.idiomatic: He often told Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, "Offices exist to keep the age in order; if the man is wrong for the post, better leave it vacant.

sentences.zh: 」太祖深然之。

translations.literal: " Grand Progenitor deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Progenitor agreed wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 大統十六年，大軍東討。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Datong, the main army marched east to punish the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Datong, the main army marched east on campaign.

sentences.zh: 柱國李弼為別道元帥，妙簡首僚，數日不定。

translations.literal: Pillar-general Li Bi was commander-in-chief on a separate route; he carefully selected his chief officers, and for several days could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar-general Li Bi was commander-in-chief on a separate route; he carefully chose his chief staff but could not settle on one for several days.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂弼曰：「為公思得一長史，無過薛端。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor said to Bi: "Thinking of a chief administrator for you, none surpasses Xue Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai told Bi, "If I am choosing a chief administrator for you, none surpasses Xue Duan.

sentences.zh: 」弼對曰：「真其才也。

translations.literal: " Bi replied: "He truly has the talent.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi replied, "He truly has the talent.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣之。

translations.literal: " He was then dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: " Duan was then sent.

sentences.zh: 加授車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was additionally granted Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書左丞，仍掌選事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to left assistant in the Masters of Writing, still in charge of selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left assistant in the Masters of Writing while still overseeing selection.

sentences.zh: 進授吏部尚書，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister of personnel and given the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of personnel and received the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 端久處選曹，雅有人倫之鑒，其所擢用，咸得其才。

translations.literal: Duan had long served in the selection bureau and had a refined discernment of men's qualities; those he promoted all had the right talent.
translations.idiomatic: Duan had long served in the selection bureau and had a refined eye for men; everyone he promoted proved fit for the task.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜軍司馬，加侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed army marshal, given the added ranks of attendant-in-ordinary, grand general of agile cavalry, and opening-office equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies, and advanced in enfeoffment to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was made army marshal with the added ranks of attendant-in-ordinary, grand general of agile cavalry, and opening-office equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies, and was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，除工部中大夫，轉民部中大夫，進爵為公，增邑通前一千八百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was made middle grand master in the Directorate of Works, transferred to middle grand master in the Ministry of Peoples, advanced in enfeoffment to duke, with a fief totaling one thousand eight hundred households together with earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, Duan was made middle grand master in the Directorate of Works, then middle grand master in the Ministry of Peoples, raised to duke, and given a fief totaling one thousand eight hundred households with earlier grants.

sentences.zh: 晉公護將廢帝，召羣官議之，端頗有同異。

translations.literal: When Duke of Jin Hu planned to depose the emperor, he summoned the officials to deliberate; Duan showed considerable disagreement.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu planned to depose the emperor, he summoned the officials to discuss it; Duan openly dissented.

sentences.zh: 護不悅，出為蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: Hu was displeased and sent him out as governor of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Hu took offense and posted him as governor of Cai.

sentences.zh: 為政寬惠，民吏愛之。

translations.literal: In government he was lenient and generous; officials and people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was lenient and generous, and officials and people alike loved him.

sentences.zh: 尋轉基州刺史。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to governor of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was posted as governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 基州地接梁、陳，事藉鎮撫，總管史寧遣司馬梁榮催令赴任。

translations.literal: Ji Province bordered Liang and Chen; affairs there required pacification and control; Governor-General Shi Ning sent army marshal Liang Rong to urge him to take up his post.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Province bordered Liang and Chen and needed firm control; Governor-General Shi Ning sent army marshal Liang Rong to hurry him to his post.

sentences.zh: 蔡州父老訴榮，請留端者千餘人。

translations.literal: More than a thousand fathers and elders of Cai petitioned Rong, asking that Duan be kept.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand elders of Cai petitioned Rong to keep Duan.

sentences.zh: 至基州，未幾卒，時年四十三。

translations.literal: After he reached Ji, before long he died, aged forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: After he reached Ji he died before long, at forty-three.

sentences.zh: 遺誡薄葬，府州贈遺，勿有所受。

translations.literal: In his final instructions he enjoined a plain burial and that no gifts from the prefecture or province be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In his final instructions he asked for a plain burial and refused any gifts from the prefecture or province.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加大將軍，追封文城郡公。

translations.literal: His former office was conferred posthumously, he was given the added rank of grand general, and posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Wencheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His former title was restored posthumously, he was promoted to grand general, and enfeoffed after death as Duke of Wencheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 諡曰質。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Zhi (Integrity).

sentences.zh: 子冑，字紹玄。

translations.literal: His son Zhou, courtesy name Shao'xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Zhou, courtesy name Shao'xuan.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏，涉獵羣書，雅達政事。

translations.literal: From childhood he was clever and keen; he ranged through many books and was accomplished in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and keen; he read widely and was skilled in administration.

sentences.zh: 起家帥都督。

translations.literal: He began his career as commander leader.
translations.idiomatic: His first appointment was as commander leader.

sentences.zh: 累遷上儀同，歷司金中大夫、徐州總管府長史、合州刺史。

translations.literal: He rose successively to high equal in protocol, and served as middle grand master in the Directorate of Revenue, chief administrator of Xuzhou Governor-General headquarters, and governor of He.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to high equal in protocol and served as middle grand master in the Directorate of Revenue, chief administrator at Xuzhou headquarters, and governor of He.

sentences.zh: 大象中，位至開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Daxi era he reached opening-office equal in protocol, grand general.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daxi era he attained the rank of opening-office grand general with equal protocol to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 端弟裕，字仁友。

translations.literal: Duan's younger brother Yu, courtesy name Renyou.
translations.idiomatic: Duan had a younger brother Yu, courtesy name Renyou.

sentences.zh: 少以孝悌聞於州裏。

translations.literal: From youth he was known in the district for filial piety and brotherly respect.
translations.idiomatic: He had been famed in the district for filial piety and brotherly devotion since boyhood.

sentences.zh: 初為太學生，時黌中多是貴游，好學者少，唯裕耽翫不倦。

translations.literal: At first he was a student at the Imperial Academy; at the time many there were sons of noble families, and few loved learning—only Yu devoted himself without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was a student at the Imperial Academy; most students there were sons of noble families and few loved learning—only Yu studied tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，辟丞相參軍事。

translations.literal: At twenty he was summoned as staff officer to the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was recruited as a staff officer in the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 是時京兆韋敻志安放逸，不干世務。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Xuan of Jingzhao had the will to dwell in seclusion and did not meddle in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Xuan of Jingzhao lived in seclusion and kept out of worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 裕慕其恬靜，數載酒肴候之，談宴終日。

translations.literal: Yu admired his tranquillity; for several years he brought wine and food to visit him and they talked and feasted all day.
translations.idiomatic: Yu admired his tranquillity; for years he brought wine and food to visit him, and they talked and feasted all day.

sentences.zh: 敻遂以從孫女妻之。

translations.literal: Xuan thereupon gave him his grand-niece in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan then gave him his grand-niece as his wife.

sentences.zh: 裕嘗謂親友曰：「大丈夫當聖明之運，而無灼然文武之用，為世所知，雖復棲棲遑遑，徒為勞苦耳。

translations.literal: Yu once said to relatives and friends: "When a great man meets an age of sage rule yet lacks clear civil and military use and is not known to the world, though he bustle and hurry, it is only vain toil.
translations.idiomatic: Yu once told relatives and friends, "When a great man lives in an age of sage rule yet lacks clear civil and military gifts and is unknown to the world, all his bustle is only wasted toil.

sentences.zh: 至如韋居士，退不丘壑，進不市朝，怡然守道，榮辱不及，何其樂也。

translations.literal: As for Master Wei, in retirement he does not hide in hills and streams; in advance he does not crowd the market and court—yet he calmly keeps the Way, untouched by glory or disgrace; how happy he is!
translations.idiomatic: Master Wei neither hides in hills and streams in retirement nor crowds the market and court in office—yet he calmly keeps the Way, untouched by glory or disgrace. What joy!

sentences.zh: 」尋遇疾而卒，時年四十一。

translations.literal: " Not long afterward he fell ill and died, aged forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he fell ill and died, at forty-one.

sentences.zh: 文章之士誄之者數人。

translations.literal: Several men of letters composed dirges for him.
translations.idiomatic: Several literary men composed dirges for him.

sentences.zh: 太祖傷惜之，贈洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor grieved for him and posthumously made him governor of Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai grieved for him and posthumously made him governor of Luo.

sentences.zh: 薛善字仲良，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Shan, courtesy name Zhongliang, was a man of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Shan, courtesy name Zhongliang, came from Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖瑚，魏河東郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hu was Wei governor of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hu was governor of Hedong commandery under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父和，南青州刺史。

translations.literal: His father He was Southern Qingzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: His father He was inspector of Southern Qing.

sentences.zh: 善少為司空府參軍事，遷儻城郡守，轉鹽池都將。

translations.literal: Shan in youth served as staff officer in the Office of the Minister of Works, was transferred to administrator of Tangcheng commandery, and became commandant of the salt ponds.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Shan served as staff officer in the Office of the Minister of Works, became administrator of Tangcheng commandery, and then commandant of the salt ponds.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，東魏

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Eastern Wei
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west, Eastern Wei

translations.literal: (Attack) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: attack]

sentences.zh: 〔改〕河東

translations.literal: [emended: changed] Hedong
translations.idiomatic: [text emended: reorganized as] Hedong

sentences.zh: （圍秦）

translations.literal: (Besiege Qin) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: besiege Qin]

sentences.zh: 〔為泰〕州，以善為別駕。

translations.literal: [emended: to Tai] Prefecture, and Shan was made vice-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Eastern Wei attacked Hedong and reorganized it as Tai Prefecture, and Shan was made vice-prefect.

sentences.zh: 善家素富，僮僕數百人。

translations.literal: Shan's family had long been wealthy; servants numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Shan's family had long been wealthy; their servants numbered several hundred.

sentences.zh: 兄元信，仗氣豪侈，每食方丈，坐客恒滿，弦歌不絕。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yuanxin was proud and extravagant; at each meal there was food for a full table, guests were always full, and zither and song never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yuanxin was proud and extravagant; every meal filled a full table, guests were always present, and zither and song never ceased.

sentences.zh: 而善獨供己率素，愛樂閒靜。

translations.literal: Shan alone provided for himself plainly and frugally, loving quiet and calm.
translations.idiomatic: Shan alone lived plainly and frugally, loving quiet and calm.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，齊神武敗幷沙苑，留善族兄崇禮守河東。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, Qi Emperor Shenwu was defeated at Shachuan; he left Shan's clansman Chongli to hold Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong, after Qi Emperor Shenwu was defeated at Shachuan, he left Shan's clansman Chongli to hold Hedong.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣李弼圍之，崇禮固守不下。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor sent Li Bi to besiege it; Chongli held firm and could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent Li Bi to besiege it; Chongli held firm and could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 善密謂崇禮曰：「高氏戎車犯順，致令主上播越。

translations.literal: Shan secretly said to Chongli: "The Gao clan's war-chariots violate righteousness and have driven our sovereign into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Shan secretly told Chongli, "The Gao clan's armies rebel against the throne and have driven our sovereign into exile.

sentences.zh: 與兄忝是衣冠緒餘，荷國榮寵。

translations.literal: Brother, we are the last threads of robe-and-cap families and have received the state's honors.
translations.idiomatic: Brother, we are the last threads of the gentry and have received the state's honors.

sentences.zh: 今大軍已臨，而兄尚欲為高氏盡力。

translations.literal: Now the great army is already at hand, yet brother still wishes to exert himself for the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: The great army is already at the gates, yet you still wish to serve the Gao clan.

sentences.zh: 若城陷之日，送首長安，云逆賊某甲之首，死而有靈，豈不歿有餘愧！

translations.literal: When the city falls, if your head is sent to Chang'an with the label "head of rebel so-and-so," would your spirit in death not be utterly ashamed!
translations.idiomatic: When the city falls and your head is sent to Chang'an labeled "head of rebel so-and-so," would your spirit not die in shame!

sentences.zh: 不如早歸誠款，雖未足以表奇節，庶獲全首領。

translations.literal: Better to submit early in good faith; though that may not suffice to show singular integrity, you may yet preserve your head.
translations.idiomatic: Better submit early in good faith; though that may not win you glory, you may yet keep your head.

sentences.zh: 」而崇禮猶持疑不決。

translations.literal: " Chongli still hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: " Chongli remained uncertain and could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 會善從弟馥妹夫高子信為防城都督，守城南面。

translations.literal: It happened that Shan's younger cousin Fu's sister's husband Gao Zixin was defense-commandant, holding the south face of the city.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Shan's younger cousin Fu's brother-in-law Gao Zixin was defense-commandant on the south face of the city.

sentences.zh: 遣馥來詣善云：「意欲應接西軍，但恐力所不制。

translations.literal: Fu was sent to see Shan, saying: "We wish to welcome the western army, but fear our strength cannot control the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was sent to tell Shan, "We wish to welcome the western army, but fear our strength is not enough to control the situation.

sentences.zh: 」善卽令弟濟將門生數十人，與信、馥等斬關引弼軍入。

translations.literal: " Shan immediately had his younger brother Ji lead several dozen students, and together with Xin, Fu, and the others cut the gate and brought Bi's army in.
translations.idiomatic: " Shan immediately had his younger brother Ji lead several dozen students; with Xin, Fu, and the others they cut the gate and admitted Bi's army.

sentences.zh: 時預謀者竝賞五等爵，善以背逆歸順，臣子常情，豈容闔門大小，俱叨封邑，遂與弟慎竝固辭不受。

translations.literal: At the time all who had taken part in the plot were rewarded with fifth-rank nobility; Shan held that turning from rebellion to obedience was the ordinary feeling of subject and son, and how could the whole household, great and small, all receive fiefs—he and his younger brother Shen firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: All who had taken part in the plot were then rewarded with fifth-rank nobility; Shan held that turning from rebellion to loyalty was the ordinary duty of a subject and son, and how could the whole household receive fiefs—he and his younger brother Shen firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，以善為汾陰令。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor commended this and made Shan magistrate of Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai commended this and made Shan magistrate of Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 善幹用強明，一郡稱最。

translations.literal: Shan was capable and forceful, clear and decisive; the whole commandery ranked him first.
translations.idiomatic: Shan was capable, forceful, and clear-minded; the whole commandery ranked his administration first.

sentences.zh: 太守王羆美之，令善兼督六縣事。

translations.literal: Administrator Wang Pi admired him and had Shan concurrently oversee affairs of six counties.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery administrator Wang Pi admired him and had Shan concurrently oversee six counties.

sentences.zh: 尋徵為行臺郎中。

translations.literal: He was soon summoned as director on the mobile headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon called to serve as director on the mobile headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 時欲廣置屯田以供軍費，乃除司農少卿，領同州夏陽縣二十屯監。

translations.literal: At the time they wished broadly to establish military colonies to supply army expenses; he was therefore made vice director of the directorate of agriculture, overseeing twenty colony supervisors in Xiachuan, Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court then wished broadly to establish military colonies to supply army expenses; he was made vice director of the directorate of agriculture, overseeing twenty colony supervisors in Xiachuan, Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又于夏陽諸山置鐵冶，復令善為冶監，每月役八千人，營造軍器。

translations.literal: Iron smelting was also set up in the mountains around Xiachuan; Shan was again made smelting supervisor, each month using eight thousand men to manufacture military equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Iron smelting was also set up in the mountains around Xiachuan; Shan was again made smelting supervisor, using eight thousand men each month to manufacture military equipment.

sentences.zh: 善親自督課，兼加慰撫，甲兵精利，而皆忘其勞苦焉。

translations.literal: Shan personally supervised the work and also added comfort and reassurance; armor and weapons were finely sharp, and yet all forgot their toil.
translations.idiomatic: Shan personally supervised the work and also comforted the men; armor and weapons were finely made, and yet the workers forgot their toil.

sentences.zh: 加通直散騎常侍，遷大丞相府從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was given the added rank of unhurried attendant at leisure and transferred to staff officer in the grand chancellor's household.
translations.idiomatic: He received the added rank of unhurried attendant at leisure and was moved to staff officer in the grand chancellor's household.

sentences.zh: 追論屯田功，賜爵龍門縣子，遷黃門侍郎，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: For past service in military colonies he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Longmen county; he was transferred to gentleman attendant at the yellow gate and given Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: For his work in military colonies he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Longmen county; he was transferred to gentleman attendant at the yellow gate and given Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 除河東郡守，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: He was made governor of Hedong commandery, promoted to grand general of agile cavalry and opening-office equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies, and given the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: He took office as governor of Hedong commandery, was raised to grand general of agile cavalry with opening-office protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, and received the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜工部中大夫，進爵博平縣公。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed middle grand master in the Directorate of Works and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Boping county.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was made middle grand master in the Directorate of Works and raised to Duke of Boping county.

sentences.zh: 尋除御正中大夫，轉民部中大夫。

translations.literal: He was soon made middle grand master in the Office of Rectification, transferred to middle grand master in the Ministry of Peoples.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made middle grand master in the Office of Rectification, then middle grand master in the Ministry of Peoples.

sentences.zh: 時晉公護執政，儀同齊軌語善云：「兵馬萬機，須歸天子，何因猶在權門。

translations.literal: At the time Duke of Jin Hu held power; Equal-in-Protocol Qi Gui said to Shan: "The myriad affairs of armies and horses must return to the Son of Heaven—why do they still rest in the gate of power?
translations.idiomatic: At the time Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu held power; Equal-in-Protocol Qi Gui told Shan, "Armies and state affairs belong to the Son of Heaven—why do they still rest in the gate of power?

sentences.zh: 」善白之。

translations.literal: " Shan reported this to Hu.
translations.idiomatic: " Shan informed Hu of this.

sentences.zh: 護乃殺軌，以善忠於己，引為中外府司馬。

translations.literal: Hu then killed Gui; because Shan was loyal to him, he was brought in as army marshal of the inner and outer headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Hu then killed Gui; because Shan had been loyal to him, he was brought in as army marshal of the inner and outer headquarters.

sentences.zh: 遷司會中大夫，副總六府事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to middle grand master in the Office of Accounting and deputy overseer of the Six Offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was made middle grand master in the Office of Accounting and deputy overseer of the Six Offices.

sentences.zh: 加授京兆尹，仍治司會。

translations.literal: He was additionally given the post of governor of Jingzhao, still administering the Office of Accounting.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made governor of Jingzhao while still administering the Office of Accounting.

sentences.zh: 出為隆州刺史，兼治益州總管府長史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as governor of Long and concurrently chief administrator of Yizhou Governor-General headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Long and concurrently chief administrator at Yizhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 徵拜少傅。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 卒于位，時年六十七。

translations.literal: He died in office at the age of sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈蒲虞勳三州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Governor of the three provinces Pu, Yu, and Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made governor of Pu, Yu, and Xun provinces.

sentences.zh: 高祖以善告齊軌事，諡曰繆公。

translations.literal: Because Gaozu knew of Shan's report on Qi Gui, his posthumous title was Duke Miu.
translations.idiomatic: Because Emperor Xiaojing knew how Shan had informed on Qi Gui, his posthumous title was Miu.

sentences.zh: 子裒嗣。

translations.literal: His son Baozi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baozi inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 官至高陽守。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Administrator of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to administrator of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 善弟慎。

translations.literal: Shan's younger brother Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Shan's younger brother was Shen.

sentences.zh: 慎字佛護，好學，能屬文，善草書。

translations.literal: Shen, styled Fohu, loved learning, could compose prose, and was skilled at cursive script.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, courtesy name Fohu, loved learning, wrote well, and excelled at cursive calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 少與同郡裴叔逸、裴諏之、柳虯、范陽盧柔、隴西李璨竝相友善。

translations.literal: In youth, together with fellow townsman Pei Shuyi, Pei Zouzhi, Liu Qiu, Fanyang Lu Rou, and Longxi Li Can, he was on close friendly terms with them all.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was close friends with fellow townsman Pei Shuyi, Pei Zouzhi, Liu Qiu, Lu Rou of Fanyang, and Li Can of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 起家丞相府墨曹參軍。

translations.literal: He began his career as ink-office adjutant in the chancellor's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as ink-office adjutant on the chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 太祖於行臺省置學，取丞郎及府佐德行明敏者充生。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor established a school at the Mobile Headquarters Secretariat, selecting administrative aides of bright virtue and keen intellect to serve as students.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai set up a school at the mobile headquarters secretariat and chose secretariat aides and staff officers of bright character and sharp mind as students.

sentences.zh: 悉令旦理公務，晚就講習，先六經，後子史。

translations.literal: All were ordered to handle official business in the morning and attend lectures in the evening, first the Six Classics, then the Masters and histories.
translations.idiomatic: They handled official business by day and studied in the evening, beginning with the Six Classics and then the Masters and histories.

sentences.zh: 又于諸生中簡德行淳懿者，侍太祖讀書。

translations.literal: From among the students, those of pure and earnest character were chosen to attend the Grand Progenitor while he read.
translations.idiomatic: From among the students he also picked those of pure and earnest character to attend him while he read.

sentences.zh: 慎與李璨及隴西李伯良、辛韶，武功蘇衡，譙郡夏侯裕，安定梁曠、梁禮，河南長孫璋，河東裴舉、薛同，滎陽鄭朝等十二人，竝應其選。

translations.literal: Shen, together with Li Can, Longxi Li Bolian, Xin Shao, Wugong Su Heng, Qiao commandery Xiahou Yu, Anding Liang Kuo and Liang Li, Henan Changsun Zhang, Hedong Pei Ju and Xue Tong, and Xingyang Zheng Chao—twelve men in all—were all selected.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was chosen along with Li Can, Li Bolian of Longxi, Xin Shao, Su Heng of Wugong, Xiahou Yu of Qiao commandery, Liang Kuo and Liang Li of Anding, Changsun Zhang of Henan, Pei Ju and Xue Tong of Hedong, and Zheng Chao of Xingyang—twelve men in all.

sentences.zh: 又以慎為學師，以知諸生課業。

translations.literal: Shen was also made school instructor to oversee the students' coursework.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was also made school instructor to supervise the students' coursework.

sentences.zh: 太祖雅好談論，幷簡名僧深識玄宗者一百人，於第內講說。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor greatly loved discourse and also selected one hundred renowned monks deeply versed in Buddhist mysteries to lecture at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai loved learned discussion and also chose one hundred eminent monks deeply versed in Buddhist doctrine to lecture at his residence.

sentences.zh: 又命慎等十二人兼學佛義，使內外俱通。

translations.literal: He also ordered Shen and the other twelve to study Buddhist doctrine as well, so that inner and outer learning would both be mastered.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Shen and the other eleven to study Buddhist teaching so they would be versed in both secular and religious learning.

sentences.zh: 由是四方競為大乘之學。

translations.literal: From this the four directions vied to pursue Mahayana learning.
translations.idiomatic: From this the realm turned eagerly to Mahayana study.

sentences.zh: 數年，復以慎為宜都公侍讀。

translations.literal: Several years later, Shen was again made tutor to the Duke of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Shen was again made tutor to the Duke of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 轉丞相府記室。

translations.literal: Transferred to recorder in the chancellor's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to recorder on the chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 魏東宮建，除太子舍人。

translations.literal: When Wei's Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed palace aide to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Palace of Wei was established, he was made palace aide to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 遷庶子，仍領舍人。

translations.literal: Promoted to junior tutor, still heading the palace aides.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to junior tutor while still heading the palace aides.

sentences.zh: 加通直散騎常侍，兼中書舍人，轉禮部郎中。

translations.literal: Added regular attendant and direct communicator, concurrently Secretariat aide, and transferred to bureau director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the added rank of regular attendant and direct communicator, served concurrently as a secretariat aide, and was transferred to bureau director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜膳部下大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed lower grand master in the Office of Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was made lower grand master in the Office of Provisions.

sentences.zh: 慎兄善又任工部。

translations.literal: Shen's elder brother Shan also served in the Office of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's elder brother Shan also held office in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 竝居清顯，時人榮之。

translations.literal: Both held clean and conspicuous posts; men of the time counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Both held honored and conspicuous posts, and contemporaries spoke of them with pride.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，除御正下大夫，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司，封淮南縣子，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was appointed lower grand master in the Office of Imperial Rectification, advanced to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Three Departments, enfeoffed Viscount of Huainan county with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Shen was made lower grand master in the Office of Imperial Rectification, promoted to grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal in three departments, and enfeoffed Viscount of Huainan with eight hundred fief households.

sentences.zh: 歷師氏、御伯中大夫。

translations.literal: He served as middle grand master in the Office of the Masters and the Office of the Guardians.
translations.idiomatic: He held successive posts as middle grand master in the Office of the Masters and the Office of the Guardians.

sentences.zh: 保定初，出為湖州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, he was sent out as Governor of Hu Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Baoding era he was sent out as governor of Hu Province.

sentences.zh: 州界旣雜蠻左，恒以劫掠為務。

translations.literal: The province's borders were mixed with barbarian tribes on the left, who constantly made raiding their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: The province bordered tribal lands, and the local chiefs lived by raiding.

sentences.zh: 慎乃集諸豪帥，具宣朝旨，仍令首領每月一參，或須言事者，不限時節。

translations.literal: Shen gathered the tribal chiefs, fully proclaimed the court's intent, and ordered the leaders to attend audience once a month; those with business to report were not limited as to time.
translations.idiomatic: Shen summoned the tribal chiefs, explained the court's policy in full, and required the leaders to attend once a month, while anyone with business to report could come at any time.

sentences.zh: 慎每引見，必殷勤勸誡，及賜酒食。

translations.literal: Whenever Shen received them in audience he earnestly counseled and admonished them and gave wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he received them he counseled them warmly, admonished them, and gave them wine and food.

sentences.zh: 一年之間，翕然從化。

translations.literal: Within a year, they swiftly submitted to transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year they had submitted to his guidance.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻乃相謂曰：「今日始知刺史真民父母也。

translations.literal: The barbarians said to one another: "Today we finally know the governor is truly the parent of the people.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen said to one another, "Today we finally know the governor is truly a parent to the people.

sentences.zh: 」莫不欣悅。

translations.literal: " None failed to rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: " All rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 自是繈負而至者，千有餘戶。

translations.literal: From then on, households arriving carrying infants on their backs numbered more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: From then on more than a thousand households came carrying infants on their backs.

sentences.zh: 蠻俗，婚娶之後，父母雖在，卽與別居。

translations.literal: Barbarian custom was that after marriage, though parents were still alive, they immediately lived separately.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal custom held that once a son married, he lived apart from his parents even while they were still alive.

sentences.zh: 慎謂守令曰：「牧守令長是化民者也，豈有其子娶妻，便與父母離析。

translations.literal: Shen told the administrators and magistrates: "Governors, prefects, and magistrates are those who transform the people; how can it be that when a son takes a wife he at once separates from his parents?
translations.idiomatic: Shen told the prefectural and county officials, "Governors and magistrates exist to transform the people. How can a son marry and at once leave his parents?

sentences.zh: 非唯氓俗之失，亦是牧守之罪。

translations.literal: This is not only a failing of the people's custom but also the fault of the local officials."
translations.idiomatic: That is not only a failing of popular custom but also a fault of those who govern."

sentences.zh: 」慎乃親自誘導，示以孝慈，並遣守令各喻所部。

translations.literal: Shen thereupon personally guided them, showing them filial piety and kindness, and also sent administrators and magistrates each to instruct their districts.
translations.idiomatic: Shen thereupon guided them himself, teaching filial piety and kindness, and sent each official to instruct his own district.

sentences.zh: 有數戶蠻，別居數年，遂還侍養，及行得果膳，歸奉父母。

translations.literal: Several barbarian households that had lived apart for years then returned to serve and support their parents; when traveling and obtaining fruit or delicacies, they brought them home to offer to their parents.
translations.idiomatic: Several tribal households that had lived apart for years returned to serve their parents, and when they obtained fruit or delicacies on the road they brought them home as offerings.

sentences.zh: 慎感其從善之速，具以狀聞。

translations.literal: Shen, moved by how quickly they turned to goodness, fully reported the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by how quickly they reformed, Shen reported the matter in full.

sentences.zh: 有詔蠲其賦役。

translations.literal: An edict exempted them from taxes and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: An edict exempted them from taxes and corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 於是風化大行，有同華俗。

translations.literal: Thereupon exemplary customs spread widely, becoming like those of the Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Exemplary customs then spread widely until they resembled those of the Chinese.

sentences.zh: 尋入為蕃部中大夫。

translations.literal: Soon recalled as middle grand master in the Office of Barbarian Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to serve as middle grand master in the Office of Barbarian Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以疾去職，卒於家。

translations.literal: He left office due to illness and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned because of illness and died at home.

sentences.zh: 有文集，頗為世所傳。

translations.literal: He had collected writings that were widely transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected writings that circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 薛善之以河東應李弼也，敬珍、敬祥亦率屬縣歸附。

translations.literal: As Xue Shan responded from Hedong to Li Bi, Jing Zhen and Jing Xiang also led their subordinate counties to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Shan answered Li Bi from Hedong, Jing Zhen and Jing Xiang also led their counties to submit.

sentences.zh: 敬珍字國寶，河東蒲阪人也，漢楊州刺史韶之十世孫。

translations.literal: Jing Zhen, styled Guobao, was a man of Puban in Hedong, tenth-generation descendant of Han Inspector of Yang Province Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Zhen, courtesy name Guobao, came from Puban in Hedong and was a tenth-generation descendant of Shao, Han inspector of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 父伯樂，州主簿，安邑令。

translations.literal: His father Bohua was provincial chief clerk and magistrate of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bohua had served as provincial chief clerk and magistrate of Anyi.

sentences.zh: 珍偉容儀，有氣俠，學業騎射，俱為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Zhen had a commanding appearance, a chivalrous spirit, and in learning, archery, and horsemanship alike was praised in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Zhen had a striking presence and a chivalrous spirit; in scholarship, archery, and horsemanship alike he was praised in his day.

sentences.zh: 祥卽珍從祖兄也，亦慷慨有大志，唯以交結英豪為務。

translations.literal: Xiang was Zhen's elder cousin; he too was magnanimous with great ambitions and devoted himself solely to befriending heroic men.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Xiang was Zhen's elder cousin; he too was open-handed and ambitious, and devoted himself to befriending heroic men.

sentences.zh: 珍與之深相友愛，每同遊處。

translations.literal: Zhen was deeply close and friendly with him; they always traveled and lodged together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was deeply attached to him, and the two always traveled and lodged together.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武趨沙苑，珍謂祥曰：「高歡迫逐乘輿，播遷關右，有識之士，孰不欲推刃於其腹中？

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu rushed toward Sha Garden, Zhen said to Xiang: "Gao Huan pursues the imperial carriage and drives it west to scatter in the Guan region; among men of discernment, who does not wish to thrust a blade into his belly?
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan rushed toward Sha Garden, Zhen said to Xiang, "Gao Huan is hounding the imperial carriage and driving the court west into the Guan region. Which man of judgment would not gladly run a blade through his belly?

sentences.zh: 但力未能制耳。

translations.literal: But our strength cannot yet restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: We simply lack the strength to stop him.

sentences.zh: 今復稱兵內侮，將逞凶逆，此誠志士效命之日，當與兄圖之。

translations.literal: Now again he raises armies to insult us from within and will unleash treacherous rebellion—this is truly the day for men of resolve to give their lives; I should plan it with you, elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: Now he raises arms again to ravage us from within and will show his treachery in full. This is the day for men of resolve to stake their lives. Elder brother, we should plan together."

sentences.zh: 」祥聞其言甚悅，曰：「計將安出？

translations.literal: Xiang heard his words and was greatly pleased, saying: "What plan do you have?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was delighted and asked, "What is your plan?"

sentences.zh: 」珍曰：「宇文丞相寬仁大度，有霸王之略，挾天子而令諸侯，已數年矣。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "Chancellor Yuwen is generous, magnanimous, and has the strategy of a hegemon; he holds the Son of Heaven and commands the feudal lords—this has gone on for years already.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "Chancellor Yuwen is generous and far-sighted, with the bearing of a hegemon. He holds the Son of Heaven and commands the lords—this has been so for years.

sentences.zh: 觀其政刑備舉，將士用命，歡雖有衆，固非其儔。

translations.literal: Look at how fully his government and punishments are in order and how officers and soldiers obey his commands; though Huan has great numbers, he is certainly no match for him.
translations.idiomatic: His government and punishments are complete, and his officers and soldiers obey without fail. Huan may have numbers, but he is no match.

sentences.zh: 況逆順理殊，將不戰而自潰矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, the righteous and the rebel differ in principle; his army will disintegrate without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness and rebellion stand on opposite grounds; his host will collapse without a battle.

sentences.zh: 我若招集義勇，斷其歸路，殲馘凶徒，使只輪不反，非直雪朝廷之恥，亦壯士封侯之業。

translations.literal: If we gather righteous volunteers, cut off his line of retreat, destroy the wicked host so that not a single wheel returns, this would not only wipe away the court's disgrace but also be the achievement by which a brave man wins a fief."
translations.idiomatic: If we gather loyal volunteers, cut off his retreat, and destroy the rebels so that not a single wheel returns, we will not only wipe away the court's shame but also win the fief that brave men seek."

sentences.zh: 」祥深然之，遂與同郡豪右張小白、樊昭賢、王玄略等舉兵，數日之中，衆至萬餘。

translations.literal: Xiang deeply agreed; thereupon with local magnates of the same commandery Zhang Xiaobai, Fan Zhaoxian, Wang Xuanlüe, and others they raised troops; within several days their force reached more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang agreed wholeheartedly. With local magnates Zhang Xiaobai, Fan Zhaoxian, Wang Xuanlüe, and others they raised troops, and within days their force exceeded ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 將襲歡後軍，兵未進而齊神武已敗。

translations.literal: They were about to attack Huan's rearguard when, before their troops advanced, Qi Shenwu had already been defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They were about to strike Huan's rearguard when, before they could move, Gao Huan had already been defeated.

sentences.zh: 珍與祥邀之，多所剋獲。

translations.literal: Zhen and Xiang intercepted him and took many captives and spoils.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Xiang intercepted the retreat and took many captives and spoils.

sentences.zh: 及李弼軍至河東，珍與小白等率猗氏、南解、北解、安邑、溫泉、虞鄉等六縣戶十餘萬歸附。

translations.literal: When Li Bi's army reached Hedong, Zhen together with Xiaobai and others led the households of six counties—Yishi, South Jie, North Jie, Anyi, Wenquan, and Yuxiang, more than one hundred thousand in all—to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Bi's army reached Hedong, Zhen with Xiaobai and the others led more than one hundred thousand households from six counties—Yishi, South Jie, North Jie, Anyi, Wenquan, and Yuxiang—to submit.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，卽拜珍平陽太守，領永寧防主；

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor praised this and at once appointed Zhen Administrator of Pingyang, overseeing Yongning garrison command;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai praised them and at once made Zhen administrator of Pingyang and commandant of Yongning garrison;

sentences.zh: 祥龍驤將軍、行臺郎中，領相里防主。

translations.literal: Xiang was made General of the Dragon Cavalry, mobile headquarters director, overseeing Xiangli garrison command.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was made general of the dragon cavalry and mobile headquarters director, with command of Xiangli garrison.

sentences.zh: 竝賜鼓吹以寵異之。

translations.literal: Both were granted military music as a mark of special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Both were granted military music as a special mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 太祖仍執珍手曰：「國家有河東之地者，卿兄弟之力。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor still took Zhen by the hand and said: "That the state holds the lands of Hedong is the work of you brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai took Zhen by the hand and said, "That the state holds Hedong is your brothers' doing.

sentences.zh: 還以此地付卿，我無東顧之憂矣。」

translations.literal: I entrust this region to you again; I need not look anxiously to the east."
translations.idiomatic: I entrust this region to you again, and I need no longer worry about the east."

sentences.zh: 久之，遷絳州刺史。

translations.literal: After some time, transferred to Governor of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to governor of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 以疾免，卒於家。

translations.literal: Relieved due to illness; died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He was relieved because of illness and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子元約，性貞正，有識學。

translations.literal: His son Yuanyue was upright by nature and had learning and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanyue was upright by nature and had real learning and judgment.

sentences.zh: 位至布憲中大夫。

translations.literal: Reached the post of middle grand master in the Office of Proclamation of Laws.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to middle grand master in the Office of Proclamation of Laws.

sentences.zh: 小白等旣與珍歸闕，太祖嘉其立效，竝任用之。

translations.literal: After Xiaobai and the others returned to court with Zhen, the Grand Progenitor praised their establishing merit and all employed them.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaobai and the others returned to court with Zhen, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai praised their service and all were given office.

sentences.zh: 後咸至郡守、刺史。

translations.literal: Later all reached posts as commandery administrator or provincial inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Later they all rose to posts as commandery administrator or provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：鄭孝穆撫寧離散，豳岐多繈負之人；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Zheng Xiaomu soothed and settled the scattered; Bin and Qi had many who came carrying infants on their backs;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Zheng Xiaomu soothed the scattered and restored order; in Bin and Qi many came carrying infants on their backs;

sentences.zh: 崔謙鎮禦邊垂，江漢流載清之詠。

translations.literal: Cui Qian guarded and defended the frontier borders; the Jiang and Han flowed with songs of his clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qian guarded the frontier, and the Jiang and Han rang with songs of his clean rule.

sentences.zh: 崔說居家理治，以嚴肅見稱，莅職當官，以猛毅為政；

translations.literal: Cui Shuo in managing the household and governing at home was famed for stern solemnity; in holding office and serving in post, he governed with fierce resolution;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shuo ran his household with stern discipline and was famed for it; in office he governed with fierce resolution;

sentences.zh: 崔猷立朝贊務，則嘉謀屢陳，出撫宣條，則威恩具舉。

translations.literal: Cui You, in standing at court to assist affairs, repeatedly offered excellent plans; when sent out to govern and proclaim regulations, both awesomeness and kindness were fully exercised.
translations.idiomatic: Cui You, when assisting at court, repeatedly offered excellent plans; when sent out to govern, he showed both stern authority and generous kindness.

sentences.zh: 裴俠忠勤奉上，廉約治身，吏不能欺，民懷其惠。

translations.literal: Pei Xia served the sovereign loyally and diligently, governed himself with frugality and restraint; clerks could not deceive him and the people cherished his bounty.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xia served loyally and diligently, lived frugally and with restraint; clerks could not deceive him, and the people cherished his kindness.

sentences.zh: 薛端歷居顯要，以彊直知名。

translations.literal: Xue Duan repeatedly held conspicuous and important posts and was known for firm uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Duan held one high post after another and was known for uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 薛善任惟繁劇，以弘益流譽。

translations.literal: Xue Shan took only heavy and arduous duties and earned flowing renown for broad benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Shan took on only the heaviest duties and won wide renown for the good he accomplished.

sentences.zh: 竝當時之良將也。

translations.literal: All were fine ministers of their age.
translations.idiomatic: All were excellent men of their time.

sentences.zh: 而善陷齊諂護以要權寵，易名為繆，斯不謬乎。

translations.literal: Yet Shan fell into slandering Qi Gui and flattering Duke of Jin Hu to seek power and favor; his title was changed to Miu—is this not apt?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shan informed on Qi Gui and flattered Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu to win power and favor; his posthumous name was changed to Miu—was that not fitting?

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
